Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. delete.description:
Revokes a token immediately and for good: the secret stops authenticating on the next request and cannot be recovered. Use it when a token has leaked — `POST …/rotate` is the one to use when the integration is staying and only the secret should change.

IRREVERSIBLE. Anonymises the caller’s account and revokes every session, including the one making the request — the session cookie is cleared in the response, so a client must treat a 200 as a logout. Confirmation is the account’s own email address in `confirm` (credentials live in Atlas, so there is no local password to re-check and a live session is what proves the human); anything else is a 400. Content the account authored is detached from it rather than deleted, so a forum thread does not lose its replies. Export first with `GET /users/me/export` — afterwards there is nothing left to export.

metadata.overview: Install the SDK, then call it.

url.description: Where deliveries are POSTed. Must be https outside development, and is called with a signature header your receiver verifies — see the webhooks guide for the scheme.

events.description: The events this endpoint should hear, by name. At least one; `GET /webhooks/events` publishes the whole vocabulary with a sample payload for each.

spaceId.description: Confine the endpoint to one space. Omitted or null means organization-wide, including spaces created after this endpoint. For a content library use `libraryId`.

libraryId.description: Confine the endpoint to one content library: `content.*` events from that library only. Not together with `spaceId`. Omitted leaves the scope as it is; null means organization-wide.

format.description: The body shape. `json` (the default) sends our own event payload; `slack` and `discord` send a message that platform renders natively, so an incoming-webhook URL from either can be pasted in with nothing in between.

categoryIds.description: Narrow delivery to events whose payload names one of these forum categories. Omitted or null means no filter — the endpoint hears the event wherever it happens.

tagIds.description: Narrow delivery to events whose payload carries one of these tags. Omitted or null means no filter. Tags are matched by name, not by id.

groupIds.description: Narrow group, user and badge events to these groups. Omitted or null means no filter; it has no effect on events that name no group.

contentTypes.description: Narrow `content.*` events to entries of these content types (by key). Omitted or null means no filter. A model change to the whole model is always delivered.

locales.description: Narrow `content.*` events to entries in these locales (BCP-47 codes, or `default` for a space's source language). Omitted or null means no filter.

bodyEncoding.description: How the delivery body is encoded. `json` (the default) POSTs `application/json`; `form` POSTs `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, for a receiver that cannot parse JSON bodies.

signatureVersion.description: Which signature headers each delivery carries. `v1` is the timestamped scheme alone and is the default for a NEW endpoint; `both` adds the legacy body-only `sha256=`, which is replayable forever and exists only for receivers not yet migrated.

kind.description: `webhook` (the default) delivers signed events. `deploy_hook` sends a plain `POST` with an EMPTY body (no signature, no payload) to a Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages or Seolyticize deploy-hook URL, on `content.*` events and the publish events `page.published`, `page.live` and `topic.published` only. Debounced: Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare one call 30 s after the last change (at most 5 min after the first); Seolyticize one call 60 s after the last publish (at most 2 min after the first), per hook, so a 30-page apply is one call. The URL is write-only: reads answer its host and `/********`. Fixed at create.

externalRef.description: Your own name for this resource (printable ASCII, no spaces, ≤200). A repeat create naming a reference already held answers that resource (200, `idempotent: true`) instead of making a second one.

metadata.description: Free-form flat tags (≤50 keys; values string, number, boolean or null), filterable on the list with `?metadata[key]=value`. The older `metadata.forgedeck_ref` is still accepted as an alias of `externalRef`.

**Replaces** the manual redirect table with `redirects` (an array, so a PATCH replaces it too) — except the rules the platform wrote itself when an entry’s path changed (`auto: true`), which are kept unless your list claims the same `from`. `?prune=true` drops those as well: the table becomes exactly the body. `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing.

The body is the manual rules. Automatic (`auto: true`) rules are kept unless a rule in the body claims the same `from`; a rule sent back exactly as read keeps its `auto` mark. Self-redirects, cycles and two rules competing for one path are refused.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

Anything other than true/false is a 422.

post.description:
What `forumulate content push` calls: run it with `dryRun` first to review the change, then without to save a new model version. Pushing an unchanged pull writes nothing; fields missing from the file are removed (restorable for 30 days).

Compares the file with the stored model. Unchanged is a no-op. Otherwise the answer lists every change on the resolved model; with `dryRun` nothing is written, without it the model is saved as a new version. A field missing from the file is removed (values hidden, restorable for 30 days); declare renames in `ops`. A Payload config is read, never run: hooks, access functions and components are reported in `issues`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

get.description:
Every space with its collections, pages and topics, as one JSON attachment — the document `POST /orgs/{orgId}/import` takes, so an export of one organization is a migration into another. CONTENT, never credentials: no tokens, no secrets, no password hashes, no webhook signing keys, so an export is safe to hand to a customer and is not sufficient to clone an installation. Streamed as it is read, so a large organization is a long response rather than a large allocation; for one that outlives a proxy timeout, take a backup (`POST /orgs/{orgId}/backups`) and download that. The per-ACCOUNT equivalent is `GET /users/me/export`.

**Requires token scope: `read`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

post.description:
Takes the document `GET /orgs/{orgId}/export` produces and lands it here. Idempotent, matched by SLUG at every level — re-importing the same document SKIPS what already exists rather than making a second copy of it — and additive: nothing in this organization is deleted because the document does not mention it. Forum spaces carry categories (tree, slugs), pins, accepted answers, polls, reactions (one row per reactor), whispers and each post’s author and `createdAt`; a post body is block `content` or `markdown`. Authors resolve to a member of this org by id, then by `members[].email`; an address with no account becomes a staged placeholder, and an account outside this org is credited by name only. The reply counts what was created and skipped per level, how each author was attributed, and lists every row that was skipped or changed in `warnings`. Synchronous: for a large forum, queue it with `POST /orgs/{orgId}/imports` instead and poll the job. For declaring the shape of a site rather than restoring content, see `PUT /orgs/{orgId}/manifest`, which dry-runs by default.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

delete.description:
Deletes the organization: it and every space in it stop answering at once, members lose access, and after a 30-day grace period the content is destroyed for good.

Without `sandbox`: a soft delete — the org and its spaces stop answering at once and the data is kept for recovery. With `?sandbox=true&confirm=<slug>`: a HARD delete for an org tagged as a sandbox (`metadata.sandbox: true`, or the older alias `metadata.forgedeck_sandbox: true`, set at `POST /orgs`) — the org and everything in it are destroyed, not recoverable, and the deletion is recorded outside the org (its own audit log goes with it). An untagged org is `409 sandbox.not_tagged` (the org is in the wrong state for this delete, like `409 sandbox.delete_blocked`); a `confirm` that is not the slug is `422 validation.failed` with `reason: confirm_required`; both with nothing changed.

**Requires token scope: `admin`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

put.description:
Replaces this space’s theme wholesale — colours, type, element styles, the phone layer. Prefer the PATCH unless you are importing a complete theme, because a full write clears anything the stored theme had that your body omits.

**Replaces** the stored theme with the body: a key you leave out is removed (use `PATCH` to change part of it). `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing; `?prune=true` adds the `diff` to a real write.

A `motion.targets` entry naming an animation that is not a built-in, a keyframe in this theme, or a keyframe of the space’s site is refused: 422 `validation.failed` naming the key and listing every valid name. The answer carries `warnings` and `ignoredInSite` like the GET — a `chrome` or `whiteLabel` written to a space that is in a site is stored and reported as `site.ignored`, because the site draws those; a logo key (`logoUrl`, `logoMark`, …) is reported as `site.overrides`, because the site’s header and footer draw the site’s. Precedence: https://forumulate.com/guides/sites#theme-precedence. A key we do not have is refused by name (422 `validation.failed`), the same answer `PUT …/theme/draft` gives; `?strict=false` drops it instead and lists every dropped key on the `X-Unrecognized-Fields` response header.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

put.summary: Replace the preset in a space

preset.description: The named layout the space's index wears. Valid values depend on the SPACE's type — see the table in this operation's description, or `GET /space-types/{type}/presets`. An unknown value is a 422 that lists the ones this type accepts.

piecePreset.description: The named layout ONE piece of the space wears. Only some types offer a choice; for the others any value is a 422 saying so. `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` lists them per type.

frontDoor.description: The front door's knobs, by key. Only the keys this SPACE's type declares, of the kind it declares — a toggle takes a boolean, a choice takes one of its values — plus `sectionOrder`. An unknown key is a 422 that names it and lists the ones this type has. `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` serves the whole set as data under `frontDoor`.

put.description:
**The layouts each type accepts.** `preset` and `piecePreset` are validated against the
space's own type, so the same word is legal for one space and a 422 for another. The same list is
served as data by `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` (and `GET /space-types/presets` for all of
them at once), which is the one to read if you are generating configuration. That route answers
FOUR vocabularies — `presets`, `piecePresets`, `shapePresets` and `frontDoor` (the keys the
type's front door accepts, and the values each one takes).

| Space type | Field | Value | What it looks like |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `guide` *(default)* | The page tree beside the writing, an on-this-page rail, and previous/next at the foot. |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `reference` | The tree and the page, nothing else — for material read in a hurry by somebody who knows why. |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `minimal` | Just the page — no tree, no rail. For docs that are really one document. |
| `DOCS` | `preset` | `landing` | A front door: your intro, a search box, and each section as a card. Pages inside keep the Guide layout. |
| `FORUM` | `preset` | `categories` *(default)* | Category cards on the way in, threads inside each. |
| `FORUM` | `preset` | `firehose` | One stream, newest first — no cards on the way in. For communities that live in the flow. |
| `FORUM` | `preset` | `dense` | The stat table a big community reads at a glance: title and tags on the left, replies, views and freshness in columns. |
| `BLOG` | `preset` | `feed` *(default)* | One column, newest first, with the standfirst under each headline. |
| `BLOG` | `preset` | `grid` | A card grid led by the cover images. |
| `BLOG` | `preset` | `magazine` | The newest post writ large, the rest as a grid beneath it. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-clean` *(default)* | Nothing beside the words; more to read waits at the end. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-toc` | An on-this-page rail to the right — for long, structured pieces. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-suggested` | Other posts down the left, magazine-style. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-rail` | Authors, date and sharing in a rail down the left; title and body beside it. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-meta-rail` | The words first, with date, read time, tags and page actions in a rail to the right. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-margin` | An offset column with a wide right margin for contents and sidenotes. |
| `BLOG` | `piecePreset` | `article-split` | The cover beside the title and standfirst, then the body. |
| `ROADMAP` | `preset` | `board` *(default)* | Columns by status, cards within them. |
| `ROADMAP` | `preset` | `list` | One column, grouped by status — reads top to bottom, best for long boards. |
| `ROADMAP` | `preset` | `timeline` | Items placed along their horizons (Now, Next, Later or Q1, Q2 …), left to right — when, not what state. |
| `CHANGELOG` | `preset` | `timeline` *(default)* | Every entry in one dated line, newest first. |
| `CHANGELOG` | `preset` | `releases` | Entries grouped under the version that shipped them. |
| `CHANGELOG` | `preset` | `gutter` | Dates in a left column on a timeline rail, each release beside its date. |
| `CHANGELOG` | `preset` | `rows` | One ruled line per release: date, type, title and tags, newest first. |
| `STATUS` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Current state on top, incident history beneath. |
| `LEGAL` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | The documents, in the order you put them, as a ruled list. |
| `LEGAL` | `preset` | `split` | A large heading and intro in a column on the left, the documents ruled on the right with a Read button each. |
| `LEGAL` | `preset` | `cards` | Each document as a card with its description, grouped under your collections — for a register of many policies. |
| `LEGAL` | `preset` | `no-front-door` | No index page — each document is its own address, linked from wherever you use it. |
| `FAQ` | `preset` | `sectioned` *(default)* | Every answer open, grouped by topic, each with an anchor to link to. |
| `FAQ` | `preset` | `accordion` | Questions closed until asked — for a long list scanned by eye. |
| `FAQ` | `preset` | `help-centre` | A search hero, category cards, popular questions and contact — each category’s questions on its own page. |
| `FAQ` | `preset` | `two-column` | Heading, intro and contact on the left, the questions as an accordion on the right — the pricing-page FAQ. |
| `CAREERS` | `preset` | `list` *(default)* | Every open role in one list, location and kind beside each. |
| `CAREERS` | `preset` | `departments` | Roles grouped under the team they join, with how many each has open. |
| `CAREERS` | `preset` | `table` | One table with a column each for team, location and type — for a long list. |
| `CAREERS` | `preset` | `cards` | Each role a card, two to a row, its facts as chips — for a handful of roles. |
| `CAREERS` | `piecePreset` | `single` *(default)* | The role, then the apply form under it, with an Apply bar that stays in reach. |
| `CAREERS` | `piecePreset` | `split` | The role beside a column that stays in view: its facts, Apply and share. |
| `CAREERS` | `piecePreset` | `tabs` | Overview and Application as two tabs — the form one click from anywhere. |
| `CONTACT` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Your words above the form, expectations beside it. |
| `CONTACT` | `preset` | `split` | Your pitch and facts on the left, the form in a card on the right that stays in view (Vercel, Intercom). |
| `CONTACT` | `preset` | `router` | Topic cards first; the form opens on the one somebody picks, or the card sends them where that topic is answered (Linear). |
| `CONTACT` | `preset` | `steps` | Email and topic first, the rest after Continue — a short first step people finish (Stripe). |
| `EVENTS` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | Upcoming events as cards with a date tile and a picture, the last few past events beneath. |
| `EVENTS` | `preset` | `luma` | Events grouped under each day, Upcoming and Past as tabs; the event page puts the cover beside the details. |
| `EVENTS` | `preset` | `community` | A month-by-month timeline with hosts and who is going; a wide banner and an RSVP bar on phones. |
| `EVENTS` | `preset` | `conference` | A grid of wide covers; each event opens on a full-width hero with a countdown. |
| `EVENTS` | `preset` | `webinar` | Rows with a video thumbnail, recordings in the past half, every time also in the reader’s zone. |
| `COURSES` | `preset` | `standard` *(default)* | A hero with the start button, modules of lessons with a progress bar, and the outline beside every lesson. |
| `COURSES` | `preset` | `tutorial` | Numbered chapters, a chapter badge over each lesson and a “Next up” card at its end. |
| `COURSES` | `preset` | `video` | A wide cover over a stats strip, and the lessons as a table with their times. |
| `COURSES` | `preset` | `cohort` | The pitch beside a sticky panel with the facts and the button; the syllabus folded by module. |
| `COURSES` | `preset` | `path` | The lessons as a winding path of nodes, with a chunky progress bar. |
| `CUSTOM` | `preset` | `landing` *(default)* | The space is one page: its address shows your home page full width, with nothing round it but your header and footer. |
| `CUSTOM` | `preset` | `pages` | A small site: each top-level page is a link in the header, and every page is full width with no sidebar. |
| `CUSTOM` | `preset` | `article` | A long read such as a security or trust page: the page tree, an on-this-page rail, a breadcrumb and the date it was updated. |
| `CONTENT` | `preset` | `headless` *(default)* | No reader of its own: your website fetches entries through the delivery API and renders them itself. |
| `ABOUT` | `preset` | `startup` *(default)* | The mission, the story and the numbers, then the team, the investors and who uses it (Linear, Vercel). |
| `ABOUT` | `preset` | `enterprise` | Scale first: the numbers, the leadership, offices on a map, awards, commitments and the legal entity (Stripe, Atlassian). |
| `ABOUT` | `preset` | `agency` | The work and who it was for, in a full-bleed banner, a logo grid, featured quotes and a gallery. |
| `ABOUT` | `preset` | `nonprofit` | The mission as a pull quote, the impact in numbers, the board and advisors, and the charity’s registration (charity: water). |
| `ABOUT` | `preset` | `open-source` | The community leads: contribution links, the maintainers in a dense grid, adopters and releases (GitLab, Rust). |
| `ABOUT` | `preset` | `personal` | A narrow, personal page: the story, the milestones newest first, where you have been featured and how to reach you. |
| `COMPARE` | `preset` | `product` *(default)* | Your product against each rival: the head-to-heads lead, then the alternatives pages and the products (Notion, Linear). |
| `COMPARE` | `preset` | `directory` | Find a product first: search, a product grid by category, then each one’s alternatives (G2, AlternativeTo). |
| `COMPARE` | `preset` | `editorial` | Roundups lead, ranked in cards with a jump list and a lede — a review site’s “best X of the year” (Wirecutter, Zapier). |

post.description:

post.description:
Allows a removed origin again, taking it back out of `fontOriginsRemoved`. The undo for the DELETE above.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

Move members from one reader identity key to another — e.g. readers who signed in through a hand-rolled `external_jwt` route keyed on your account id, now signing in through your IdP keyed on `(iss, sub)`. Body: `{from:{provider, issuer?}, to:{provider, issuer}, map:[{externalId, sub, ext?, principal?}] (≤50,000) | mapUrl (https NDJSON), onConflict: "stop"|"merge", idempotencyKey?}`. Providers are reader-auth methods (`external_jwt`, `oidc`, `atlas_byo`, alias `atlas`). An `oidc` → `atlas_byo` switch where the sub is already the external id needs no map. DRY RUN by default; `?apply=true` writes. Answers 202 with a job in the shared job model (`kind: member.relink`, `state` queued → running → completed|failed; also at `GET /orgs/{orgId}/jobs/{jobId}`, announced once as `job.completed`) whose `result` is `{dryRun, matched, unmatched[], conflicts[], merged[], unchanged, totals:{before, after}}`. Two external ids mapped to one sub are merged into one member (content re-owned, points and standing summed, principals joined); a sub already held by another member is a conflict unless `onConflict: "merge"`. Idempotent: the same key and body answers the first job, and re-running a finished map reports every row `unchanged`. Each relinked member is audited as `member.relinked` with the token that asked.

**Requires token scope: `admin`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

Move a public roadmap here from Canny or Featurebase: send their export (CSV or JSON) and it is queued as a roadmap board, items in the matching lanes with their votes, comments, tags and ETA.

Body `{ source: "canny" | "featurebase", data, space?: { name, slug } }`. `data` is the export as the source wrote it: a CSV file’s text, or its JSON (Canny `{ posts, comments?, votes? }`; Featurebase `{ submissions | results, comments? }`, or a bare array of posts). Each post becomes a roadmap item: open / under review → SUBMITTED, planned → PLANNED, in progress → IN_PROGRESS, complete → SHIPPED, closed / rejected → DECLINED, anything else SUBMITTED (listed in `notes`). Named voters become votes by those people; the rest of the source’s count is kept as anonymous votes. A multi-board export makes one board per source board. Answers 202 with the job to poll at `GET /orgs/{orgId}/imports/{jobId}`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

get.summary: Get a queued import

post.description:
Step 1 of 3. Body `{ source: "discourse" | "phpbb" | "vbulletin" | "flarum" | "discord", spaceId | space: { name, slug }, tablePrefix?, columnMap?, permalinks? }`. Answers the job (`status: "uploading"`). Step 2: send the export with `POST …/forum-imports/{id}/files`, in parts of at most 8,000,000 characters. Step 3: `POST …/forum-imports/{id}/start` with `{ dryRun: true }` to count everything and list every row that would be skipped without writing, then `{ dryRun: false }` to import. Poll `GET …/forum-imports/{id}` for `progress` and the `report`. Accepted exports. **discourse**: the backup’s `dump.sql` (pg_dump; the console extracts it from the `.tar.gz`), or its tables as CSV files named by table (`users.csv`, `user_emails.csv`, `categories.csv`, `topics.csv`, `posts.csv`, `tags.csv`, `topic_tags.csv`, `post_actions.csv`, `topic_custom_fields.csv`, `post_custom_fields.csv`, and the reactions plugin’s `discourse_reactions_reactions.csv` / `discourse_reactions_reaction_users.csv`), or one JSON object of those tables (`{ "users": [...], "topics": [...], "posts": [...] }`), or topic JSON as the Discourse API answers `/t/{id}.json`. **phpbb** (3.0–3.3): a mysqldump `.sql` or CSV/JSON of `users`, `forums`, `topics`, `posts` (+ `thanks` / `posts_likes`), table prefix `phpbb_` by default. **vbulletin**: 4 — `user`, `forum`, `thread`, `post`, `tag`, `tagcontent`, `post_thanks`, `reputation`; 5 — `node`, `text`, `channel`, `tagnode`, `tag`, `privatemessage`, `reputation`. **flarum**: `users`, `tags`, `discussions`, `posts`, `discussion_tag`, `post_likes` (+ `reactions` / `post_reactions`). **discord**: DiscordChatExporter JSON (`--format Json --include-threads All`), one file per forum thread. A `.sql` dump is read without a database server (MySQL `INSERT` with or without column lists, and pg_dump `COPY`). Columns named differently are mapped with `columnMap` (`{ "posts": { "post_text": "body" } }`). What is imported: categories (nested), tags, users (matched to members by email, else staged accounts claimed on sign-up; users without an email are credited by name), topics and replies with their original dates, likes and reactions, the accepted answer, pinned/closed/archived state, and permalinks from the old addresses (`/t/slug/123`, `/viewtopic.php?t=12`, `/showthread.php?12-title`, `/d/12-slug`…) to the new topics, categories, profiles and tags. Images and attachments are copied into the organization’s files: Discourse uploads from the backup (the dry-run report lists them in `uploadsNeeded`; send each as a file named by its backup path, `uploads/…`, base64-encoded, before the real run), and attachment links (Discord’s CDN, Flarum fof/upload, and phpBB/vBulletin attachments when `oldBaseUrl` names the old forum) fetched from public addresses only; a file that cannot be copied stays a link and is listed. Discord members (no email) become one staged account each, keyed by their Discord id; `POST …/forum-imports/claims` hands one to a member. Re-running the same export (or a newer one) skips what an earlier run imported and adds only new topics and replies.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

The pages a change adds or edits (as Markdown, front matter allowed — the publish converter reads them) and the slugs it removes, stored as a preview named `name` (`pr-123`). Answers a tokened link on the space’s own addresses that shows the space as the change would publish it: edited pages in their new form, new pages at their new address, removed pages flagged, every other page as published. Also a per-page diff summary (added / changed / removed / unchanged, lines added and removed against the published text) and `comment`, a ready-made pull-request comment. The same `name` again replaces the pages (or with `append: true` adds to them) and renews the link for `ttlDays` (default `previews.ttl_days`, 7) — the token stays the same, so the PR comment does not change. A revoked preview pushed again gets a new link. The pages are never published and never reach search, sitemaps or feeds; the link is never cached at the edge.

Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

post.description:
Creates a page directly inside one collection, which is the usual authoring door: it saves you creating a page and then moving it, and the slug is derived from the title unless you name one.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

**A taken slug is reported, not hidden.** With `onSlugTaken: "suffix"` a page whose slug already exists is created at `slug-2`, and the response says so: `slugChanged: { asked, used }` plus a sentence in `warnings[]` and on the `X-Field-Warnings` header. `onSlugTaken: "fail"` gives a `409 page.slug_taken` instead. **Unset, it is versioned:** `suffix` for a caller stating a `Forumulate-Version` before `2026-12-01` (or none), `fail` from `2026-12-01` — the safe default, and the blog's. `PATCH …/pages/{pageId}` takes the same option with the SAME default, so one rule covers both doors. See [Slugs](https://forumulate.com/guides/api-conventions#slugs).

**Send ONE body field.** `content` (block JSON) is exclusive with `body` and `sections` (Markdown); sending `content` alongside either is a 422 naming both. It used to accept them together and silently discard the block document. `body` and `sections` together remain legal — that is the designed authoring path (slots first, then trailing prose).

**A `parentId` must exist here.** A page id that is not a live page in this space is a 404, and one in another collection is a 422. A nil uuid used to be stored, producing a row that never appeared in the tree.

**A `sections` key must be a slot this space type declares.** An unknown key is a 422 listing the slots that exist; it used to create one that nothing renders.

**Same job, other door:** A docs page in a given collection; Item_create makes one piece of any space type from its shape, Import_importFiles brings in many files at once.

get.description:
Read a page: its id, metadata, `status` (`published`/`draft`), and a stable `contentHash` of the published body — so a docs-as-code pipeline can detect drift (a UI edit since it last pushed) without downloading the document. Add `?include=content` to also get the live block document as `content`.

**Requires token scope: `read`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

`status` is derived from the LIVE revision (`published` once anything has been published), so it does not change when a newer draft is saved — read `hasDraft` and `draftUpdatedAt` for that. Both were missing, and a pipeline reading `published` on a page whose latest work was unpublished had no way to tell.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. **Requires token scope: `read`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a trashed page: its content, every revision, draft and checkpoint, its comments and feedback, its live-collaboration document and its search and AI index entries. Its translations and other versions are separate pages and stay. Irreversible — there is no undo and nothing to restore from. Only a page already in the trash (`DELETE …/pages/{pageId}`) can be destroyed: a live page is a 409 `destroy.not_trashed`, and a page id from another space is a 404. Requires `?confirm=<the page slug>`; a missing or wrong slug is a 422 `validation.failed` with `reason: confirm_required` and nothing is deleted. To drop cached copies instead, use `Cache_purgePage`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

Existing operation pages are MOVED and RENAMED in place — their ids and bodies are kept, and every changed address gets an automatic 308 redirect; only tag and landing pages are created or deleted. For a spec that declares none (`servers: null`) or names a host readers must not call. An absolute URL, a relative one (`/v1`) or a template (`https://{region}.api.example.com`). A path’s or operation’s own `servers` still win where the spec declares them. Recorded on the registered spec, so every resync (and the auto-resync) keeps it; an import without it goes back to the spec’s own. The stored copy of the spec is never edited.

The uploaded `file` may be **JSON or YAML** — the same reader the inline `spec` field and the `sourceUrl` fetch use. It used to be `JSON.parse` alone, answering 400 "convert a YAML spec to JSON first", which is how most people keep a spec. A file that parses but is not an OpenAPI document (no `openapi`/`swagger`, nothing to generate from) is a 422 here too, rather than an empty reference written with a 200.

`mode` is `single | per-operation | per-tag` and `onExisting` is `fail | skip | replace` (default `fail` — this importer writes generated pages in one transaction, so refusing costs nothing and is all-or-nothing). Both used to be cast through unchecked, so a bogus `mode` silently took the single-page branch. `dryRun` and `replaceCollection` take the boolean spellings above; anything else is a 422.

post.description:
Writes a batch of pages from Markdown or block JSON in one transaction, creating the collections they need. The door a migration or a git sync drives; it reports what it would do first if you ask for a dry run.

Imports Markdown files into a collection. **`onExisting` defaults to `replace`**: a file whose slug the space already has OVERWRITES that page (kept for existing callers). Send `onExisting: "fail"` or `"skip"` to protect existing pages, and `dryRun: true` first to read the per-file `plan` — creates, replaces, collisions and what a `prune` would remove — with nothing written.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

`onExisting` is `fail | replace | skip | rename | duplicate` and defaults to `replace` (this importer syncs authored files per file, and the first import of a repo routinely lands on the starter page a new space ships with). **An unrecognised value is now a 422** — it used to fall through to `replace`, so a typo chose the destructive option. `fail` refuses to write over an existing page, counts it in `failed`, lists its slug in `refused[]`, and keeps `prune` from deleting it.

On the multipart doors, `dryRun` and the rest are read exactly as strictly as the JSON fields of the same name: `true/false/1/0/yes/no/on/off`, and anything else is a 422. `dryRun=maybe` used to run a REAL import.

**Same job, other door:** Many files at once; one piece is Item_create (any space type) or Collection_createPage (a docs page in a collection).

200.description: Import counters. `files` is how many files the request carried — the denominator. `created` (new pages), `replaced` (existing pages rewritten in place), `skipped` (left untouched) and `failed` (could not be turned into a page) are DISJOINT and satisfy `created + replaced + skipped + failed === files`. `imported` is NOT "files processed": it is a convenience total meaning `created + replaced` — the pages this run actually wrote — so it EXCLUDES skipped and failed, and it OVERLAPS `replaced`. That overlap is why three files all rewritten answer `files: 3, created: 0, replaced: 3, imported: 3`: three pages, not six. Sum the disjoint four; never add `imported` to `replaced`. (An earlier version of this page documented `imported + replaced + skipped + failed === files.length`; that invariant is withdrawn — it stopped being true once a replace began counting as an import.) `collisions`/`prunedSlugs`/`plan`/`dryRun` appear when the request asks for them. `redirects` and `retired` appear when a file DECLARED an address change: see the request body for `slug:` and `redirect_from:`. `redirects` lists the rules the run wrote into the space's redirect table; `retired` lists the slugs it moved to the trash because a rule took over their address (reversible with `POST …/{pageId}/restore`). On a dry run both say what WOULD happen and nothing is written.

onExisting.description: What to do about a slug the SPACE already has (resolved space-wide, never per-collection): `replace` (the default) updates the existing page in place; `fail` writes nothing over it and lists its slug under `refused` (the default of `POST …/openapi/import`, offered here so one explicit value makes both importers behave identically); `skip` leaves it untouched; `rename` is the ONLY value that auto-suffixes to a free slug like `getting-started-2` (opt-in — a page at a URL nobody wrote is the worst docs-as-code outcome); `duplicate` is the legacy spelling of `rename`. An unrecognised value is a 422, never a silent `replace`.

prune.description: Sync mode. After importing, soft-delete (to trash) every live page in this scope the run did not create/replace/skip — so deleting a source file makes its published page disappear. `collection` scopes to the target collection; `space` to the whole space.

dryRun.description: Plan only. Returns what WOULD happen — the same counts (`imported` counts creates AND replaces, so `imported`+`skipped`+`failed` == files.length and `replaced` is a subset of `imported`), a per-file `plan`, cross-collection `collisions`, and the `prunedSlugs` a prune would remove — and writes nothing. `dryRun: true` sets `dryRun` on the response.

purge.description: What to drop from the cache once the page is live. `page` (the default) purges this page's every address; `space` purges everything under the space (do this when a title in the navigation changed, so every page's sidebar shows it); `none` leaves the CDN as it is (our own web tier is still refreshed). The answer's `purged` says which addresses went and which `edge` took them — `none` when no CDN fronts them. Works with every CDN the org has configured (`GET /orgs/{orgId}/integrations/cdn`), not only Cloudflare.

syncBaseline.description: Record what this publish made live as the page's sync baseline, so a later docs-as-code publish can tell an edit made since (in the studio, through the API) from its own and refuse to overwrite it. `forumulate publish` always sends it. See `GET …/spaces/{spaceId}/sync-state`.

schema.description:
**A Markdown file may declare its own address.** Two frontmatter keys are read, and unknown keys are still ignored:

- `slug:` — the address this file lands at, instead of the one its filename spells. Slugified, so `Billing & Plans` and `billing-and-plans` are the same address; a value with nothing a URL can hold in it is refused with the file named, never quietly renamed. Two files declaring one slug is a `422`.
- `redirect_from:` — the addresses this page REPLACES, comma-separated, each rooted and relative to the space's mount (`/old-page`, never `/docs/old-page` — the reader prepends the mount itself). The import writes a redirect rule for each one and moves the page that answered there to the trash, because a rule alone leaves the old page in the sitemap, `llms.txt` and search. Both are reported on the response as `redirects` and `retired`. A self-redirect, a duplicate or a loop is a `422`, exactly as it is on `PUT …/redirects`; an operator's own manual rule for that address is left alone.

get.description:
One window of a content type’s entries in one locale, filtered by `where`, ordered by `sort` and walked by cursor (`page.nextCursor` while `page.hasMore`). References are populated to `depth`. A `where` or `sort` on a field that is not indexed is served only on a small type; past that it is a 422 naming the field to index. Locales: a list holds ONE row per entry, read through the fallback chain like a one-entry read: the entry’s twin in `locale` when it has one, otherwise its twin in the first chain locale that has one, otherwise the source. With `fallback=false` only entries that have a twin in `locale` are listed. `where` and `sort` read the listed twin’s OWN localized values (a localized field that twin left empty — filled in the response from the rest of the chain — matches as absent and sorts as missing) and the source entry’s non-localized values. Each row’s `locale` says which twin was listed; `count=true` counts the same rows.

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: `{field: {operator: value}}` with `and`/`or` lists, as JSON or bracket-encoded (`where[price][gt]=10`). Operators: equals, not_equals, in, not_in, contains, like, exists, gt, gte, lt, lte, near.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated field paths, `-` first for descending. Default: the type’s `defaultSort`, else `-updatedAt`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per window, 1–100 (default 20; above 100 is capped).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous window. A cursor from a different sort is a 422.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Ask for `page.total`; sent only where counting is cheap.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A locale code (the library’s source locale when omitted). `*` on a one-entry or global read returns every locale under `localized`.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Fall back through the declared locale chain, then the source (default `true`). Whole entry: a locale with no twin serves the first twin of its chain. Per field: an empty localized field — and an empty localized leaf inside a localized group, array or blocks row, matched by row id — is filled from the first entry of the chain that has it. Non-localized fields always come from the source entry. `false`: only the asked locale, empty fields left empty.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: How far references are populated: 0 serves stubs `{kind, id, contentType, slug}`. Default 1; capped by the plan’s reference depth (a larger value is a 422).

parameters.name: populate
parameters.description: Per type, the fields to keep on a populated entry: `populate[author]=name,avatar`.

parameters.name: select
parameters.description: Comma-separated field paths to keep in `fields`.

parameters.name: draft
parameters.description: Accepted for a preview key, which always reads drafts; a delivery key asking for drafts is a 403.

parameters.name: libraryId
parameters.description: The library id. UUID only: this address carries no `{orgId}` to resolve a content library slug inside.

200.description: The domain, verified. anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

anyOf.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

data.overview: Install the SDK, then call it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

A live key is revoked (or, where its organization set `security.leaked_key_response: notify`, left live and reported), its owner is emailed and every organization it reaches gets an audit row; nothing is lost but the key itself. label.description: What readers see ("AI & ML" for `ai-ml`). The slug stays the id. `null` = the slug.

color.description: Chip background: a hex value or a CSS colour name.

colorDark.description: Chip background in a dark scheme. `null` = `color` in both schemes.

textColorDark.description: Chip text colour in a dark scheme. `null` = `textColor` in both schemes.

gradient.description: Gradient ink through the tag’s words (the `text` and `eyebrow` looks, a card kicker): 2–3 `#hex` stops. `null` clears.

description.description: Shown on the tag’s landing page and as its meta description.

pageScheme.description: The colour scheme the tag’s landing page and its posts wear; `null` = the space’s.

pagePalette.description: Theme palette slots for those pages (`primary`, `background`, …).

coverUrl.description: The image heading the tag’s landing page.

anyOf.description: An icon name from `GET /icons?for=header` (see the `HeaderIconName` enum: our glyphs, the extended set and the brand marks), or an image URL (https://…, /api/assets/…, or a data: PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF — not SVG). Any other bare word is refused.

icon.description: A glyph name (the theming guide lists them) or an image URL drawn before the tag’s label, on the blog and the forum. `null` = none.

parent.description: The tag this one sits under (hierarchical categories). `null` = top level.

translations.description: The label and description per locale (`{ "de": { "label": "KI" } }`). `null` clears them.

internal.description: An internal tag (Ghost’s `#tag`): groups posts for the owner and is never shown to a reader.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

sections.description: Markdown per section of the piece, keyed by the section key its shape declares. A BLOG article ships two, BOTH REQUIRED: `standfirst` (the line listings and link previews show) and `body` (the post). A space can add or rename its own — the keys for one are at `GET /space-types/{type}/slots` (and the space’s own shape). Combined with `markdown`, which follows the sections as ordinary prose.

onThisPage.description: Whether THIS piece carries the "on this page" rail: `auto` (the surface default), `always` or `never`. Beats the space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` clears it back to the space’s.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

sections.description: Markdown per section of the piece, keyed by the section key its shape declares. A BLOG article ships two, BOTH REQUIRED: `standfirst` (the line listings and link previews show) and `body` (the post). A space can add or rename its own — the keys for one are at `GET /space-types/{type}/slots` (and the space’s own shape). Combined with `markdown`, which follows the sections as ordinary prose.

Opens or closes comments on ONE post — `{ "enabled": false }` hides the existing ones and refuses new ones with a 403. It is not the door that creates a comment, and it is not `comment-settings`, which governs comments on a PAGE; this is the per-post switch.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: `true` holds the answer (up to 60 s) until the reader SERVES the published version — read through the reader past the edge — and adds `live` `{live, url, version, servedAt, waitedMs, retryAfter, reason}`. Not live in time: `202` with `Retry-After` and `live.live: false` — the same body as the success, the publish itself done (the `page.live` webhook still fires when it is served); read `live.retryAfter` or subscribe to `page.live`. Absent or `false`: answers at once, as before, and never 202.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`): read, merge and validate exactly as the write would, store NOTHING, and answer the would-be result with `dryRun: true` and `diff` — every key it would `add`, `remove` or `change` (`{path, op, from?, to?}`, sorted by path; secrets appear only as `<key>Set`). Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

postAs.description: Moderators only (`forum.moderate`; 403 otherwise). `org` publishes the topic under the organization: its name, and its email-branding logo as the picture. `self` (the default) is the posting account. Cannot be combined with `byline` or `bylines` (422). Readers see the byline in place of the account on the topic and in the list; the console and API keep `authorId`, so the post stays accountable to a person.

byline.description: Moderators only. The name (with optional `url`, `avatarUrl`) the topic is published under, as on a blog post. `null` is the posting account.

bylines.description: Moderators only. Credits in order, as on a blog post: `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <key>}` from this space’s author registry (`PUT /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/blog/authors/{key}`; an unknown key is a 422). The first entry is what readers see as the author.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of results to return, 1-based. Out-of-range pages return an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page — the spelling used everywhere else in this API. This endpoint also accepts `pageSize`, which it has always taken; `limit` wins if both are sent. Defaults to 25. 100 is the most it serves — a larger value is capped, not refused, and a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

get.summary: Get the search in a space (public reader forum)
get.description: Takes no credential. Answers 200 with { `hits`, `minQueryLength` }. Query: `q`. Applies to FORUM spaces.

Operators: category:<slug>, tag:<t>, tags:a,b, -tag:<t>, status:solved|unsolved|open|closed|archived|noreplies, in:title|pinned|tagged|untagged (plus in:bookmarks|watching|tracking|muted|seen|unseen when signed in), topic:<id> (search within one topic: the hit carries its matching `posts`), @author, before:/after:YYYY-MM-DD, created:, order:latest|top|views|latest_topic, min_views:, min_posts:. `total` counts the whole matched set; `hits` is one page of it. `titleHighlight` and `snippet` mark matched words between U+E000 and U+E001 (plain text, never HTML).

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: The space: its uuid, or its slug within the organization. An id further down the path that belongs to a DIFFERENT space is a 404, not a cross-space read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Hits per page. Defaults to 20. 50 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Hits skipped. Defaults to 0. 1000 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 0 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

200.description:
Success.

This answer carries no `page` object: the forum's operator search (F-162): ranked per request like the unified search above, so it publishes `offset` into a ranking and `total` for the matched set rather than a cursor into a collection. `?limit=` caps how much of the ranking you get; there is no cursor to walk, and `hasMore` would have nothing true to say.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

get.summary: Get the forum in a space (public reader)
get.description:
The forum’s front page for a visitor: its categories, the pinned topics and the most recent activity, with nothing a reader may not see. No token is needed on a public space, which is what makes it the door a static site or a mobile app reads. `?locale=` lists each topic under its published translation in that declared language (NUM-43).

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Defaults to 25. 100 is the most it serves — a larger value is capped, not refused, and a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Published releases matching `q`, newest relevance first. `path` is the release page under the changelog's own address.

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: The space: its uuid, or its slug within the organization. An id further down the path that belongs to a DIFFERENT space is a 404, not a cross-space read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

get.description:
The events a member can see in this space, upcoming or all. The read behind a public calendar or an "what is on" block; drafts are excluded unless the caller may manage them.

**Requires token scope: `read`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: The space: its uuid, or its slug within the organization. An id further down the path that belongs to a DIFFERENT space is a 404, not a cross-space read.

data.description: The created resource again, under a key that is the same on every create — so a generic client needs one parser rather than one per endpoint. It is the SAME object as the key named after the resource (`page`, `article`, `topic`, …), which remains the canonical name.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

timezone.description: IANA time-zone name the event is published in, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

coverAlt.description: What the cover shows, for screen readers and link previews.

stateReason.description: Why it was cancelled or postponed — shown in the banner on the event page.

joinLinkVisibility.description: `public` (default) or `attendees`: only readers who RSVP `going` get the join link.

tags.description: Tag slugs. Labels and colours come from the space’s tag registry, like a blog’s.

hosts.description: Who hosts it, in order: `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?}` or `{author: <key>}` from the space’s author registry (`…/spaces/{spaceId}/authors`).

rsvpApproval.description: A `going` waits as `pending` until staff approve it. Default false.

guestsMax.description: How many guests (+1s) one RSVP may bring. Default 0.

questions.description: Registration questions (the Forms field model), answered when RSVPing `going`.

recurrence.description: Repeat this event: `{freq: daily|weekly|monthly, interval?, byWeekday?, count?, until?}`. Each later date becomes its own event (own RSVPs) in the series; `null` stops the series. Only on an event that is not itself a generated date.

seriesScope.description: On a series’ first event: `following` also applies this change to every date still to come. Default `this`.

gallery.description: Photos from the event, shown on its page once it is over.

recapUrl.description: The write-up: a blog post (a path on this site or a URL), linked once it is over.

feedbackFormId.description: A form of this organization (Forms) asked of readers once the event is over.

noindex.description: Keep this event out of search engines. Default false.

featured.description: Pin it to the top of the calendar. Default false.

publishAt.description: A PUBLISHED event stays off every public door until this instant; subscribers are told then.

rsvpOpensAt.description: RSVPs open at this instant. Null = now.

rsvpClosesAt.description: RSVPs close at this instant. Null = when the event is over.

hideVenueUntilRsvp.description: Withhold the address (page, .ics, JSON-LD) until the reader RSVPs `going`.

venueNotes.description: Directions, parking, which door — shown under the place.

streamUrl.description: An embeddable livestream (YouTube, Vimeo, any https player), shown while it is live.

reminders.description: This event's reminder leads; `[]` sends none; `null` uses the space's setting.

customFields.description: The organizer’s own facts, shown with the others: `[{label, value}]`.

terms.description: Terms a reader must accept to RSVP (Markdown). Null = none.

password.description: Write-only: the page asks for this password. `null` removes it.

rsvpGroups.description: Org groups whose members may RSVP. Empty = anybody who can read the event.

replayGated.description: The recording is shown only to readers who RSVP’d `going`.

attendanceCertificates.description: A certificate of attendance for every checked-in attendee.

colistOn.description: Other EVENTS spaces of this organization whose calendars list this event too.

live.description: The live room’s parts: chat, emoji reactions, the attendee directory, 1:1 networking, points.

translations.description: The event in other languages: `{"de": {title, description, …}}`. Null removes them.

discoverable.description: List the event in the public discovery directory (published, public events only).

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

get.description:
Requires the `forum.read` capability in this organization or space. Answers 200 with { `speakers`, `page`, `data` }. Pages with `limit` and `cursor` (state `Forumulate-Version` for the `page` envelope). Applies to EVENTS spaces.

**Requires token scope: `read`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

200.description: A grounded answer, streamed. Frames are NAMED (`token`, `citations`, `done`, `error`), so subscribe per event rather than with `onmessage`. Prose arrives token by token; the `citations` frame carries the anchor-level sources for what was just said; `done` carries the `queryId` to rate the answer with. An error after the first token arrives as an `error` FRAME, not as a status — the status is already committed — and the client falls back to the blocking `docs/ask`.

put.description:
**Replaces** the stored AI provider with the body: a key you leave out is removed (use `PATCH` to change part of it). `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing; `?prune=true` adds the `diff` to a real write.

For organization admins: connects the organization's own AI provider and key (AI is bring-your-own-key, there is no platform key), which turns on the AI assistant, summaries, questionnaires and other AI features.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`): read, merge and validate exactly as the write would, store NOTHING, and answer the would-be result with `dryRun: true` and `diff` — every key it would `add`, `remove` or `change` (`{path, op, from?, to?}`, sorted by path; secrets appear only as `<key>Set`). Anything other than true/false is a 422.

parameters.name: prune
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`): the stored object becomes EXACTLY this body — every key you leave out is removed — and the answer carries `diff` naming what changed, removals included. Combine with `dryRun=true` to read that diff first.

put.description:
The sign-in methods readers of this organization may use: Google, Microsoft, Apple, an OIDC provider of your own, or none. Configure it before making a space members-only, or there is no way in.

**Replaces** the stored reader sign-in registry with the body: a key you leave out is removed (use `PATCH` to change part of it). `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing; `?prune=true` adds the `diff` to a real write.

Secrets are never lost by omission: a secret key (`clientSecret`, `secret`, `sharedSecret`, `secretKey`, `bindPassword`, `outboundSync.scimBearerToken`) that is absent, empty, or a redaction mask (`********`) keeps the stored value, and the `<key>Set` / `secretSet` markers a read returns are ignored — so a GET can be sent back verbatim. Providers are matched to stored ones by `method` + `order`, then by `method` alone. To change part of the registry without resending anything, use PATCH. Secret values are stored encrypted at rest and are never returned, in plaintext or encrypted form. Every IdP provider (`oidc` with a `config.preset` such as auth0, clerk, okta, cognito, keycloak, entra, google, firebase, supabase, workos, or `atlas_byo` — `{method:"atlas", config:{instanceId, audience}}` is accepted as its shorthand) carries an output-only `resolved`: `{preset, issuer, jwksUri, discoveryUrl, audience, tokenUse, maxTokenTtlSec, signInUrl, backchannelLogoutUrl, lifecycleEventsUrl}`, or `error: {reason, message}` when discovery failed. It is ignored on write. The answer carries `warnings[]` (`sign_in_url_overrides_providers`, `signin_url_unreachable`, `sign_in_url_return_to_unconfirmed`): heads-ups, never a refusal. A method this save leaves configured nowhere in the organization signs out the readers who came in through it.

**Requires token scope: `admin`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

Deep merge. Top-level keys: absent keeps, `null` deletes, a value sets. Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.
