state.description: An incident walks investigating → identified → monitoring → resolved. Maintenance may say the same steps in its own words — scheduled, in_progress, verifying, completed — which are stored as those four (`maintenanceState` reads them back).

severity.description: `notice` is informational — it moves no component and paints no day unless you link components with an impact. `maintenance` is the one severity with a scheduled window.

body.description: The incident write-up as a block document — or as a Markdown string, converted like a page body. Or send `markdown`.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

components.description: The components this incident affects, each with its impact. While the incident is open each one reads at least that state, and the days it spans take that colour on the component’s bars. Sent, it replaces the set; `[]` clears it.

startedAt.description: When the incident actually began, if not when it was posted. Clamped to now; a backfill is about the past.

resolvedAt.description: When it ended — only on an incident that is (or is being made) `resolved`. Posting one already resolved marks it Retroactive on the public page.

autoStart.description: Maintenance: move to in progress at `scheduledFor` (default true). Subscribers are told.

autoComplete.description: Maintenance: complete at `scheduledUntil` (default true). Off, it stays in progress until you complete it — for work you verify by hand.

audience.description: Who may see this on the public page: `everyone` (default), `signedIn` (any signed-in reader) or `groups` (a signed-in member of one of `groups`). Hidden rows are dropped by the API before anything is sent. The machine doors — `summary.json`, `api/v2`, the feeds, the badge and the widget — always answer as an anonymous reader.

notifySubscribers.description: Email the page's confirmed subscribers and push to its Slack/Discord/webhook channels. Default true. Delivery is queued, so the response does not wait for it. On PATCH, only a state change is announced.

tone.description: This incident’s card accent on the page, a palette slot. Null: the colour of its state.

pinned.description: Pin it above everything else on the page — in the active band while open, first in the history once resolved — until unpinned.

hideFromHistory.description: Keep it out of the public history, the archive and the feeds once it is resolved (a test incident, a mistaken post). It still colours the days it spanned.

bannerText.description: The banner's headline while this incident is open, in your words ("Payments are delayed in the EU"). Null: the built-in headline for the page's state.

recurrence.description: Maintenance only: when this window completes, the next one is scheduled — the same title, write-up, components and length, a week or a month later — until `until`. Null stops it.

post.description:
An `http` check is UP when the request connected AND the response status is below 400 (2xx and 3xx both pass); a `keyword` additionally requires that term in the body, and `certExpiryDays` requires that many days left on the TLS certificate. Set `expectStatus` (100-599) and that EXACT code becomes the only status that counts as up — anything else, 200 included, is down — which is how you watch a dependency whose healthy unauthenticated answer is a 401 or a 405. Null (the default) keeps the under-400 rule. Like `keyword` and `certExpiryDays`, it applies to `http` checks only — a `heartbeat` monitor has no response to inspect and is UP while the job has pinged within `intervalSeconds`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

kind.description: `http` (default) polls `url`; `heartbeat` waits for your job to ping; `manual` is probed by nothing — its state is `declaredState` (else operational) or what an open incident linked to it says; `space` rolls up another status page of this organization (`targetSpaceId`) on a hub page; `statuspage` mirrors a vendor’s public Statuspage (`url`, plus `vendorComponent`). Fixed at creation: a PATCH cannot turn one kind into another — delete and re-create instead.

targetSpaceId.description: Kind `space`: the status page it rolls up (state, uptime and days are that page’s).

vendorComponent.description: Kind `statuspage`: the vendor component’s id or exact name in its summary.json. Null: the vendor page’s overall indicator.

region.description: Where it runs ("EU", "US-East"). `theme.status.components.groupBy: region` groups by it.

description.description: What the component is, in a sentence — shown to readers beside its name.

slug.description: Its stable address within the page (component page, per-component subscription), normalised to lowercase words joined by hyphens. Minted from the name on create when omitted; unique per page — a taken one is a 409. Renaming the component does not move it.

linkUrl.description: Where the component’s own docs or product live; its name links there.

display.description: `bars` (default) draws its day bars; `status` only its state; `hidden-unless-degraded` leaves it off the page while it is operational.

startsOn.description: The day it started existing. Earlier days draw as "not yet" rather than as no data. Null: from its first check (a `manual` component: from the day it was created).

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds between checks (`http`, clamped to 30–3600, default 60) or the longest wait for a ping (`heartbeat`, clamped to 60–604800, default 3600). PATCH clamps by the same rule.

keywordAbsent.description: Invert `keyword`: the check FAILS while the term is in the body ("error", "maintenance mode") — Better Stack's "keyword absent". Default false.

probe.description: What a protocol monitor probes (kinds tcp, udp, icmp, dns, tls, smtp, imap, pop3, domain, browser): `host` (+ `port`), a DNS `record`/`resolver`/`expect`, the `days` a certificate or registration must have left, a browser check’s `url` and `selector`. Validated per kind; every host must resolve to a public address.

regions.description: Probe regions this component is checked from (`GET …/status/regions`). Empty: the primary checker only.

confirmRegions.description: How many regions must see it failing before it reads down (capped at how many report). Default 1.

barDays.description: Its own day strip length on the board; null follows the theme’s `bars.days`.

showUptime.description: Show its uptime figure beside the strip. Default true.

paused.description: Stop probing without deleting: the row and its history stay on the page, no new checks are taken and no alert is sent, and the component reads `unknown` (or its `declaredState`) until it is resumed. `alertsEnabled: false` only mutes the alerts while the probe keeps running.

audience.description: Who may see this on the public page: `everyone` (default), `signedIn` (any signed-in reader) or `groups` (a signed-in member of one of `groups`). Hidden rows are dropped by the API before anything is sent. The machine doors — `summary.json`, `api/v2`, the feeds, the badge and the widget — always answer as an anonymous reader.

declaredState.description: A state a person declares, which wins over the checks until it is cleared with `null`. Every field of this body — this one, `alertsEnabled` and both thresholds included — is applied on create exactly as on PATCH.

externalRef.description: Your own name for this resource (printable ASCII, no spaces, ≤200). A repeat create naming a reference already held answers that resource (200, `idempotent: true`) instead of making a second one.

metadata.description: Free-form flat tags (≤50 keys; values string, number, boolean or null), filterable on the list with `?metadata[key]=value`. The older `metadata.forgedeck_ref` is still accepted as an alias of `externalRef`.

probe.description: What a protocol monitor probes (kinds tcp, udp, icmp, dns, tls, smtp, imap, pop3, domain, browser): `host` (+ `port`), a DNS `record`/`resolver`/`expect`, the `days` a certificate or registration must have left, a browser check’s `url` and `selector`. Validated per kind; every host must resolve to a public address.

regions.description: Probe regions this component is checked from (`GET …/status/regions`). Empty: the primary checker only.

confirmRegions.description: How many regions must see it failing before it reads down (capped at how many report). Default 1.

barDays.description: Its own day strip length on the board; null follows the theme’s `bars.days`.

showUptime.description: Show its uptime figure beside the strip. Default true.

paused.description: Stop probing without deleting: the row and its history stay on the page, no new checks are taken and no alert is sent, and the component reads `unknown` (or its `declaredState`) until it is resumed. `alertsEnabled: false` only mutes the alerts while the probe keeps running.

audience.description: Who may see this on the public page: `everyone` (default), `signedIn` (any signed-in reader) or `groups` (a signed-in member of one of `groups`). Hidden rows are dropped by the API before anything is sent. The machine doors — `summary.json`, `api/v2`, the feeds, the badge and the widget — always answer as an anonymous reader.

declaredState.description: A state a person declares, which wins over the checks until it is cleared with `null`. Every field of this body — this one, `alertsEnabled` and both thresholds included — is applied on create exactly as on PATCH.

metadata.description: Free-form flat tags (≤50 keys; values string, number, boolean or null), filterable on the list with `?metadata[key]=value`. The older `metadata.forgedeck_ref` is still accepted as an alias of `externalRef`.

maintenanceReminderHours.description: Hours before a scheduled maintenance window that confirmed subscribers are reminded of it (0 = never). Default 24. Only a window announced further ahead than this is reminded — one posted an hour before needs no reminder.

autoTranslate.description: Languages every incident is machine-translated into as it is posted and updated, with the organization’s own translation provider (Settings → DeepL). A translation a person wrote is never overwritten.

maintenanceReminders.description: Hours before a scheduled maintenance window that confirmed subscribers are reminded, up to three (72 and 1, say). Each is sent once. `[]` sends none. Replaces `maintenanceReminderHours`, which still reads back as the first.

maintenanceNotifyStart.description: Tell subscribers when a maintenance window starts. Default true.

maintenanceNotifyEnd.description: Tell subscribers when a maintenance window completes. Default true.

suppressAlertsInMaintenance.description: No operator alert (and no automatic incident) for a component while a maintenance window that affects it is in progress — the deploy that takes the health check down is expected. Default true.

smsTemplate.description: The SMS text sent to phone subscribers, with {page} {title} {state} {url} filled in. Null: the built-in line ("{page}: {title} — {state}. {url}").

replyTo.description: Where a subscriber's reply to a status email goes. Null: the organization's mail default.

alertChannels.description: Which channels readers may subscribe through, each on (default) or off. A channel switched off is not offered on the page, a new subscription through it is refused, and existing ones stop receiving notices.

uptimeExcludesMaintenance.description: Maintenance is not downtime (default true). False: a maintenance window costs the days of the manual components it affects like an outage does.

dayThresholds.description: This page's own day-colour floors: a day on the uptime bar is operational at or above `operational`%, partial at or above `partial`%, an outage below. `null` clears them so the page follows the org's `status.day_thresholds` (default 99.9 / 99). stateSource.description: Where this page's component states come from. `current`: the latest checks — what every reference status page reports; the uptime window stays on the page as the percentage and the bars. `window`: the latest checks, then a poor uptime window degrades a passing check (under 99.5% degraded, under 97% partial outage). `null` clears it so the page follows the org's `status.state_source` (default `current`).

state.description: An incident walks investigating → identified → monitoring → resolved. Maintenance may say the same steps in its own words — scheduled, in_progress, verifying, completed — which are stored as those four (`maintenanceState` reads them back).

severity.description: `notice` is informational — it moves no component and paints no day unless you link components with an impact. `maintenance` is the one severity with a scheduled window.

body.description: The incident write-up as a block document — or as a Markdown string, converted like a page body. Or send `markdown`.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

components.description: The components this incident affects, each with its impact. While the incident is open each one reads at least that state, and the days it spans take that colour on the component’s bars. Sent, it replaces the set; `[]` clears it.

startedAt.description: When the incident actually began, if not when it was posted. Clamped to now; a backfill is about the past.

resolvedAt.description: When it ended — only on an incident that is (or is being made) `resolved`. Posting one already resolved marks it Retroactive on the public page.

autoStart.description: Maintenance: move to in progress at `scheduledFor` (default true). Subscribers are told.

autoComplete.description: Maintenance: complete at `scheduledUntil` (default true). Off, it stays in progress until you complete it — for work you verify by hand.

audience.description: Who may see this on the public page: `everyone` (default), `signedIn` (any signed-in reader) or `groups` (a signed-in member of one of `groups`). Hidden rows are dropped by the API before anything is sent. The machine doors — `summary.json`, `api/v2`, the feeds, the badge and the widget — always answer as an anonymous reader.

notifySubscribers.description: Email the page's confirmed subscribers and push to its Slack/Discord/webhook channels. Default true. Delivery is queued, so the response does not wait for it. On PATCH, only a state change is announced.

tone.description: This incident’s card accent on the page, a palette slot. Null: the colour of its state.

pinned.description: Pin it above everything else on the page — in the active band while open, first in the history once resolved — until unpinned.

hideFromHistory.description: Keep it out of the public history, the archive and the feeds once it is resolved (a test incident, a mistaken post). It still colours the days it spanned.

bannerText.description: The banner's headline while this incident is open, in your words ("Payments are delayed in the EU"). Null: the built-in headline for the page's state.

recurrence.description: Maintenance only: when this window completes, the next one is scheduled — the same title, write-up, components and length, a week or a month later — until `until`. Null stops it.

published.description: False: a draft — on the console only, told to nobody, until `POST …/incidents/{id}/publish`. Default true.

notifyAt.description: Post now, tell subscribers later: the notice goes out at this time instead (Statuspage’s delayed notifications).

get.description: `overall` and each component's `status` are the REPORTED state, and three things decide it, in this order: a human's `declaredState` always wins; then the latest checks (a run of failures reaching the monitor's threshold is a `major_outage`, a shorter run `degraded`); then — only when the board's `stateSource` is `window` — measured history may degrade a passing check: under 99.5% uptime reads `degraded` and under 97% `partial_outage`, once `window.sufficient` is true (at least 20 checks spanning at least 6 hours). `stateSource` is the page's own setting, else the org's `status.state_source`, else `current` (the latest checks only, what reference status pages report). History only ever degrades, never improves. `uptimeOver` is each component's uptime over its newest 30, 60 and 90 days. `window` says what each percentage was actually measured over — `samples`, `daysCovered`, `spanHours` and the first/last check — because `uptime` alone was being printed beside a hardcoded '90 days'. `historyDays` are the day keys the `history` arrays line up with, oldest first. `outages` are the failing runs our own checks recorded, longer than each monitor's `failureThreshold`, whether or not anybody opened an incident for them.

get.description: statuspage.io's `summary.json` shape, derived from the same board a person reads so the two cannot disagree. Components keep OUR state words (`degraded`, `maintenance`, `unknown`) and carry Statuspage's `id`, `description`, `position`, `group_id` (plus `group_name` and `slug`); `incidents` are the open ones with `id`, `impact`, `shortlink` and `incident_updates`; `scheduled_maintenances` lists maintenance not yet over; `page` has `id`, `time_zone` and `updated_at`. The Statuspage-worded twin is `…/status/api/v2/summary.json`. `uptime` is nullable (null means nothing was recorded, which is NOT 0%) and each component carries the `window` its percentage was measured over, so a poller can tell '100% over ninety days' from '100% over ninety minutes'. `outages` lists the failing runs our own checks recorded even when no incident was opened. The snake_case keys inside `incidents` are deliberate Statuspage compatibility, not our envelope drifting.

get.summary: Record a heartbeat for a monitor
get.description: Takes no credential. Answers 200 with { `ok` }. Query: `detail`, `status`, `ok`.

parameters.name: monitorId
parameters.description: The monitor id. UUID only.

requestBody.description: Optional — an empty POST is a clean run, exactly as before. Report a run that did not go cleanly so the component reads degraded or partial instead of going silent (which reads as an outage after 1.5x the interval). Lenient by design: a body that cannot be read is treated as a clean run, never refused. The same three fields are accepted as query parameters. `metrics` (`{"lagSeconds": 42}`, up to 20 finite numbers) feeds the monitor's `metricThresholds`: a value above `degradedAbove` reads degraded, above `downAbove` down, whatever the sender said (never better than it said); the newest values draw the component's sparkline.

ok.description: `false` = the job ran but part of it failed: the component reads partial_outage while pings keep arriving. Ignored when `status` is a known state.

status.description: Name the state outright. `degraded` / `partial_outage` keep the job counted as up but colour the component; `major_outage` (or `down`) records a failed check now instead of waiting for silence; `up` is a clean run. The next clean ping clears it.

detail.description: What went wrong, in the job’s words (up to 500 characters). Shown to the organization in the console beside the monitor, not on the public page. Dropped on a clean run.

metrics.description: Numbers the job measured, by name (letters, digits, `_ . -`). Read against the monitor's `metricThresholds`; an unreadable entry is dropped, never refused.

post.summary: Record a heartbeat for a monitor, by POST
post.description: A heartbeat from a scheduled job saying it ran: the signed URL is the whole credential, so a cron line or a CI step can call it with nothing else. Wire it into the job itself — a monitor that has never been pinged reports unknown rather than down. A run that partly failed can say so with `{"ok": false, "detail": "…"}` instead of going silent.

Records a restart window against the monitor, so the uptime history shows a dip a 60-second poll could never have caught. The token is the same secret as the monitor's heartbeat ping URL. Answers `{ ok: true }` when the report was accepted — including a restart folded into a window reported in the last 30 seconds, which is already on the board — and `{ ok: false }` for a bad token or an unknown monitor.

patch.description:
Merges into the stored override: `add`/`set`/`omit`/`order` and the space settings you send are applied, and anything you omit is left as it was. Applying the same patch twice is the same as applying it once.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: The space: its uuid, or its slug within the organization. An id further down the path that belongs to a DIFFERENT space is a 404, not a cross-space read.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: spaceId

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Which page shape to apply. A shape adds named slots to what a piece of this space is made of; it is NOT the reader layout (that is `PUT …/preset`). `how-to` — One task, done. The goal, what you need first, the steps, and how to tell it worked. `tutorial` — Learning by building something end to end — for somebody who does not know the product yet. `reference` — What something is and exactly how it behaves — read in a hurry, by somebody who already knows why. `explanation` — Why something works the way it does — the page that stops the same question being asked forever. `troubleshooting` — One symptom, its cause, and the fix — written for somebody who is already annoyed. `bug-report` — What happened, what should have happened, and how to see it — the three things a fix needs. `feature-request` — The problem first, then the idea — so somebody can solve it a better way than you asked for. `question` — Asks for the context, what was already tried, and what was expected — the three things a good answer needs. `landing` — A wide opening statement, then the three things you want somebody to do next. `comparison` — Two things, side by side, and the honest sentence about when to pick each. `release` — What shipped, what it changes for a reader, and what to do if it broke something. `keepachangelog` — The standard changelog categories — Added, Changed, Fixed, and the rest — one list each. `incident` — What broke, who it hit, what you did, and what stops it happening again. `role` — The work, who it suits, what it pays, and how to apply. `policy` — A plain-English summary over the document itself, so somebody can read either. `announcement` — One thing, said properly: what it is, why now, and what a reader does about it. `faq-answer` — The answer first, then the reason, for the question you keep being asked. `contact-sales` — Who to talk to about buying, how fast they answer, and what to have ready. `contact-support` — How to get help fastest, what to send with a report, and when somebody answers. `drop` — A drop: its release day (apart from the publish date), price, style code, colourway, retailers, regions and status — drawn as a Release details block, on the calendar and in Product JSON-LD. `roundup` — A post that lists the releases in a window — this week, next month, or between two days — and stays right without hand-editing.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

anyOf.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

after.overview: Install the SDK, then call it.

before.overview: Install the SDK, then call it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

get.summary: Get the chrome in a space
get.description: The furniture a given page actually wears — header, footer, announcement, resolved theme and the alternates a visitor may pick. For a space inside a site it reports the site’s, with the space theme layered over it, because that is what renders; the space’s own stored header is kept and deliberately unused.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: The space: its uuid, or its slug within the organization. An id further down the path that belongs to a DIFFERENT space is a 404, not a cross-space read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Updates per page, newest last. Defaults to 20. 100 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

get.summary: List updates in a space
get.description: From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

get.description: Where a reader's "Sign in" button sends the browser: a redirect to the space's identity provider (`method` picks google, microsoft, apple, oidc or atlas_byo). `returnTo` must be one of the space's own addresses or it is refused with 422; omitted, it is the verified custom domain.

302.description: The provider’s answer, verified; the reader session is set.

Location.description: The validated `returnTo`. When the destination is on another origin, it is instead a `…/visitor-oidc/adopt` URL on that origin carrying a one-time signed ticket, because a cookie cannot be set cross-origin.

get.summary: Handle the visitor OIDC callback
get.description: The single redirect URI a customer registers with their reader identity provider; the space travels in signed state. Exchanges the code, provisions the member when accounts are on, sets the reader pass and returns them to `returnTo` — via the adopt ticket when that is another domain.

302.description: Adopts the session handed over by the callback. A bad, expired or already-used ticket ALSO redirects rather than erroring: this URL is in a reader’s address bar, and an error page there is a dead end where the sign-in page is a way forward.

Location.description: The `returnTo` the ticket carries, or the reader mount’s own root when it cannot be read.

get.summary: Adopt the visitor OIDC
get.description: Redeems the single-use 60-second handoff ticket the reader OIDC callback issues when sign-in finished on a customer's own domain, so the cookies are set by that host. Reached under the space mount; a spent, expired or forged ticket just redirects on.

post.description: Revokes every session the reader sign-in created (ours and the Atlas session) and clears every reader cookie on the host that answers: `forumulate_session`, `fm_signed_in`, every `cflx_vis_<spaceId>` and `cflx_vis_org_<orgId>` the request carries (and, on Forumulate hosts, the Atlas `__session`/`__atlas_rt`/`__atlas_uat`). Call it SAME-ORIGIN — `https://<your-domain><mount>/_api/public/reader/sign-out` — because a host-only cookie can only be cleared by its own host. The body is optional: with `orgId` + `spaceId`, `redirectTo` is the space's `signOutUrl` carrying `returnTo` (or the validated `returnTo` when none is set). A plain HTML form post is answered `303` to that address.

200.description: `{ ok: true, cleared: string[], redirectTo: string | null }` — `cleared` names every cookie this response expired.

It revokes the reader session and clears every reader cookie on that host, exactly as the POST does, then answers `302`. `returnTo` may be an address of the space, or an https URL on the origin of the space's reader-auth `signInUrl` or `signOutUrl` (your product); anything else, or none, lands on the space's primary address. Without `orgId`/`spaceId` it lands on the mount root and `returnTo` is ignored. `orgId` and `spaceId` take an id or a slug.

post.description: OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0 receiver for reader sign-in. Any IdP configured as a reader sign-in provider of this organization (Atlas, Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, any OIDC provider) posts `logout_token` here (application/x-www-form-urlencoded; JSON is accepted too). The token is verified against the issuer's JWKS; `aud` must be the provider's audience or client id; `events` must carry `http://schemas.openid.net/event/backchannel-logout`; no `nonce`; `sid` or `sub`. The reader sessions it names end server-side — the session row is revoked and the visitor cookie refused — so the cookies on the customer's domain stop working on the next request. 200 when done (or nothing was signed in), 400 with `error.reason` for a token we will not act on.

post.description: One receiver for every IdP. `{preset}` is `atlas`, `clerk`, `workos`, `auth0`, `okta` or `generic` (the normalized shape, Standard Webhooks signed). The delivery is verified with the scheme the preset names (or the provider's `webhookScheme`: standard_webhooks, workos, bearer, hmac_sha256) and the provider's write-only `webhookSecret`, then mapped to user.updated, user.banned, user.unbanned, user.deleted or session.revoked and applied under the keys `reader.idp_user_banned`, `reader.idp_user_deleted` and `reader.idp_deletion_grace_days`. Events we have no use for answer 200 `type: "ignored"` so the sender does not retry. `?issuer=` picks one provider when several share a preset.

401.description: No reader is signed in on this host (`auth.unauthenticated`). There is nobody to identify.

403.description: Asked from another site (`Sec-Fetch-Site` neither `same-origin` nor `none`; `error.reason: cross_site`). Ask from the reader page itself.

404.description: Signed in, but nothing can be minted; the error envelope's reason says why: `not_an_idp_sign_in`, `no_consent_provider` (the space's provider takes no identity token), `unknown_issuer`, `issuer_not_anchored` (we never vouch for an issuer an organization could have claimed), `signing_not_configured`, or an IdP decline (`integration_not_enabled`, `session_inactive`, …). parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The tag you believe this resource is at: the `ETag` header the matching read sets. It is opaque and changes on any change to the resource (body, title, slug, `locale`, metadata). The `contentHash` that read returned is also accepted and guards the content only — it does not move on a metadata edit. The write is applied only if the tag still holds, so two editors cannot overwrite each other unnoticed. A list is accepted and any member matching is enough; `*` asserts only that the resource exists. Omit it and the write is unconditional. On every other route a concrete value is a 428 rather than silently ignored.

It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Accepted only by `/connector/kb/*` and by the public reader of the spaces it names; every management route answers it 401 `reason: wrong_audience`. `audience` is a free-form label (e.g. `chatly`, `intercom`, `zendesk`, `custom`). post.description:
Request a scoped, expiring credential for a partner product — a consent platform, a DSAR orchestrator, a chat or knowledge vendor, a referral program, a status aggregator; any vendor, the `partner` field is a label. Body: `{ partner, resource: "org:<id or slug>", scopes, space_ids?, expires_at?, metadata? }`. Answers the link, `client_secret` (shown ONCE — store it in the partner product) and the `token_endpoint` the partner exchanges it at (OAuth2 client_credentials, one-hour tokens). Default expiry one year, which is also the most a link may have (FMU-SI10): `expires_at` must be within 365 days and `null` (never) is refused; the owners are e-mailed 30, 7 and 1 days before it lapses.

**Requires token scope: `admin`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

post.description: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749), `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or JSON. Two grants. `grant_type=client_credentials` with a partner link’s `client_id` + `client_secret` (HTTP Basic or form) and an optional `scope` narrowing the link’s scopes → a one-hour access token for the surfaces that accept that scope. `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` (RFC 8693) with `subject_token` (a JWT from an OIDC issuer the organization trusts — `POST /orgs/{org}/operator-issuers`), `resource=org:<id or slug>`, optional `audience=forumulate` and `scope` (`read`, `write`, `admin`; default `read write`) → a one-hour token acting as the linked operator in that ONE organization; root actions additionally need the IdP to have reported a second factor within 5 minutes (`403 auth.step_up_required`). Errors are RFC-shaped: `{ error, error_description }` — `invalid_request` for a malformed request (a missing or repeated parameter, an unsupported `subject_token_type`/`requested_token_type`), `invalid_client` (401) for failed client authentication (an unknown client, a wrong secret, a revoked or expired link — never told apart), `unauthorized_client` (400) with `error_description: "partner link pending approval: …"` and `approval_url` for the CORRECT secret of a link an owner has not approved yet, `invalid_grant` for a subject token that is not a JWT, untrusted, badly signed, expired, without `exp`, unlinked or whose person is no longer a member, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_scope`, or `invalid_target` for a `resource`/`audience` naming no organization. Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

patch.description:
Deep-merges into the stored configuration, so renaming the call-to-action cannot discard the theme beside it. Nested objects combine, ordered lists and plain values replace, and an explicit null erases a key — the same rules the space theme patch follows. Add `?dryRun=true` to see the key-by-key diff without writing.

**Deep-merges** the body into the stored site config: nested objects merge, arrays and scalars replace, and `null` deletes a key; the merged result is then validated as a whole, exactly as `PUT` validates. `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing.

Deep-merges `config`. Inside a site the site theme is the base every member space layers over key by key; `chrome` keys and `whiteLabel` are the site’s outright, and the header and footer draw the site’s logos. A space’s `GET …/theme?view=effective` names the layer behind every key. Precedence table: https://forumulate.com/guides/sites#theme-precedence.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

**Same job, other door:** `config.seo` is the same object SiteSettings_setSeo writes, and `config` holds the site navigation (headerLinks, headerSpaceIds, tabs, navMenu, desktopNav, mobileNav, subnav, topBar); one space's SEO is SpaceSettings_patchSeo, one page's Page_setMetadata.

get.summary: Get the site’s robots.txt rules

put.description:
**Replaces** the stored site robots.txt rules with the body: a key you leave out is removed (use `PATCH` to change part of it). `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing; `?prune=true` adds the `diff` to a real write.

`siteId` is the site’s uuid (`GET /orgs/{orgId}/sites`). Replaces the owner’s rules: `extraRules`, `disallowPaths`, `aiCrawlers` / `aiCrawlerPolicy`, `sitemaps`, `extraSitemaps` and a `raw` block (a key left out is cleared). Merge order: the generated private-path disallows are always kept, then the AI-crawler policy, `extraRules`, `disallowPaths`, sitemaps, `raw`. Takes effect on the site’s robots.txt within seconds, on every address the site is served at.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

parameters.description: The site: its uuid, or its slug within the organization.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`): read, merge and validate exactly as the write would, store NOTHING, and answer the would-be result with `dryRun: true` and `diff` — every key it would `add`, `remove` or `change` (`{path, op, from?, to?}`, sorted by path; secrets appear only as `<key>Set`). Anything other than true/false is a 422.

parameters.name: prune
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`): the stored object becomes EXACTLY this body — every key you leave out is removed — and the answer carries `diff` naming what changed, removals included. Combine with `dryRun=true` to read that diff first.

get.summary: Get the site (public reader)
get.description: What an anonymous visitor is served for a whole site: its configuration, the member spaces, their published page trees and the tabs they are grouped into. One request for the navigation of everything under the address, which is why a reader shell fetches it first. `?nav=lean` keeps `id`, `slug`, `title`, `icon`; past 200 pages only top-level ones, with `more` counts; `lean-all` lists every level.

Every space the site publishes — docs and API reference pages, blog posts, forum topics, changelog releases, roadmap ideas, legal documents, status incidents and opted-in events — in one ranked list. `types=post,topic` and `spaces=<slug|id>,…` filter it; an unknown value is a 422 naming the legal ones. Each hit carries an absolute `url` (the customer’s own domain when the space or site has one), its `kind`, and a `breadcrumb`. When nothing matches as typed, one typo per word of four letters or more is corrected against the site’s own words and `corrected` says so (`search.typo_tolerance`). `answer=true` adds a grounded answer citing the hits when the org turned one on (`search.site_answer`). Anonymous answers are `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60` (`search.site_cache_seconds`); one shaped by a signed-in reader is `private, no-store`. Searching records nothing: report a settled search with `POST …/search-events` once the visitor’s consent allows it. `minQueryLength` is the org’s floor: a shorter term answers no hits rather than an error.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Hits per page. Defaults to 20. 50 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Hits skipped. Defaults to 0. 1000 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 0 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: answer
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

200.description:
Success.

This answer carries no `page` object: relevance-ranked hits for one query across a site’s spaces (FMU-B12), fused per request; `offset` walks the ranking, a cursor would name a row the next query does not have. `?limit=` caps how much of the ranking you get; there is no cursor to walk, and `hasMore` would have nothing true to say.

`connected: false` when none. Never the secret: `secretHint` is its last four characters. `presets` lists the vendors with a preset; `custom` is any other service. We POST `{version: 1, question, locale, site: {id, slug, name, orgId}, sources: [{ref, kind, title, url, text}]}` and read `{answer: string|null, answered?: boolean, citations?: [ref]}`. Every request carries `Forumulate-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex hmac-sha256(secret, "<t>.<body>")>` and the secret as `Authorization: Bearer` (or your `headerName`). Only `ref`s we sent are kept as citations.

**Replaces** the stored answer provider with the body: a key you leave out is removed (use `PATCH` to change part of it). `?dryRun=true` answers the result and its `diff` without storing; `?prune=true` adds the `diff` to a real write.

get.description:
Every request opened in this organization through the executor contract, oldest change first: ordered by `updatedAt`, then `id`, and paged at the source. Answers `{data, page}` — the rows once under `data`, with `page.hasMore` and `page.nextCursor`; pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` to continue. No `total`: walk on `hasMore`. A request that changes during a walk moves to the end, so walking to `hasMore: false` sees the latest state of every request. `since` (ISO date-time) keeps requests UPDATED at or after it — a finished request counts as changed — which is the reconciliation sweep: remember when you started the last walk and send it as `since`. `status` and `type` take one value or a comma list (`status=pending,scheduled`). Organization-scoped, authorised by the executor key (or a partner link with `privacy:execute`), like every executor route.

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. get.description:
Answers `{"enabled": false}` rather than 404 when no credential is configured. `enabled` is true for a minted key, or for a live partner link holding `privacy:execute` (`auth: "partner_link"`, the credential a consent platform connected with `PUT …/consent {connect:{partnerLink}}` uses; no key is minted then). Never returns the secret: `prefix` is its hint (`forumulate_live_exec_AbCd…WxYz`), enough to tell keys apart; a key minted before hints were kept answers its fingerprint, `sha256:` and the first 12 hex of the SHA-256 of the key. `lastUsedAt`/`lastUsedBy` (the caller’s User-Agent) show which orchestrator holds it; `previousKeyValidUntil` is set while a rotated-out key is still in its grace window. `executorUrl` is the base a rights orchestrator drives (lookup → open → poll → export).

post.description:
Generates a new executor credential for `/privacy/executor/{orgId}/*` and returns the secret ONCE — only its hash is stored, so a lost secret is rotated rather than recovered. Calling this again replaces the previous credential: it stops working immediately, or after `graceMinutes` (up to a week) so the orchestrator can be updated without a gap. A new credential expires a year after it is minted (`expiresAt`); the organization’s owners are e-mailed 30, 7 and 1 days before. Use `GET privacy/executor-key` for the key’s metadata, `POST privacy/executor-key/test` to check it.

**Partner platforms** (no Forumulate token): send the partner signature header instead (`CookieMunch-Partner-Signature: t=<unix s>,kid=<kid>,ed25519=<base64url>` over `<t>.<raw body>`) with the body `{ partner, externalId, cbid, orgId, nonce, iat }` — `partner` is `forumulate`, `externalId` this organization’s id (or slug), `cbid` a site this organization configured with that platform, `nonce` never reused. The signature is verified against the partner’s published JWKS, `t` may be at most five minutes old, the nonce is single-use, and the grant is confirmed with the partner before anything is minted. Answers `{ secret, executorUrl, prefix, previousKeyValidUntil }`; the previous key keeps working for an hour. 401 for a bad, stale or replayed signature (`reason`), 403 when the organization has not chosen the partner, names another account or another site, or switched executor keys off for it (`PUT /orgs/{orgId}/consent/partners/{partnerId}` with `allowExecutorKey: false`), 503 when the grant cannot be confirmed.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

post.description:
Registers Forumulate with Cookie Munch as this organization’s rights executor (contract v2), server to server, adopting or replacing the `forumulate` connection it already holds for this site, whoever registered it (`action`: create | adopt | replace). Cookie Munch is asked to mint the executor key itself under its partner link (`mintFrom: forumulate`); when it cannot, Forumulate rotates the key (the old one works for another hour) and sends it — and if Cookie Munch then refuses, the rotation is undone, so the key it held stays current. `?dryRun=true` answers the plan (`wouldMint`, `existingConnection`, `action`) after checking the key and the site, and changes nothing. `orgProvisioningKey` is a Cookie Munch key with `dsar:write`, used for this request only and never stored. `cbid` defaults to the site in the organization’s Cookie Munch consent config. Answers the link status; no secret is ever returned.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

post.description:
Provider-agnostic inbound consent/DSAR webhook. A customer on ANY CMP points their subscription here and configures the signing secret (`webhookSecret`, or POST `consent/webhook-secret`). Authenticity is the HMAC signature over the raw body, verified with THIS org's secret. Use THIS endpoint for every provider; `/hooks/cookiemunch` is the legacy platform-managed path only.

**Partner platforms** need no secret: send `CookieMunch-Partner-Signature: t=<unix s>,kid=<kid>,ed25519=<base64url>` (or the header your platform is registered with) over `<t>.<raw body>`. It is verified with the key named by `kid` in the partner's published JWKS; a `t` more than five minutes old (or a minute ahead) is refused; the organization must have chosen the partner (as its consent provider, or at `PUT /orgs/{orgId}/consent/partners/{partnerId}`), `externalId` must name it and `cbid` a site it configured. A verified partner delivery answers `{ ok, partner, event, verifiedAt }` and flips `webhookConfigured`/`webhookVerifiedAt` on `GET /orgs/{orgId}/consent`. A request carrying an HMAC signature header, to an organization with a secret, is verified by the HMAC as before.

get.description:
Every request opened in this organization through the executor contract, oldest change first: ordered by `updatedAt`, then `id`, and paged at the source. Answers `{data, page}` — the rows once under `data`, with `page.hasMore` and `page.nextCursor`; pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` to continue. No `total`: walk on `hasMore`. A request that changes during a walk moves to the end, so walking to `hasMore: false` sees the latest state of every request. `since` (ISO date-time) keeps requests UPDATED at or after it — a finished request counts as changed — which is the reconciliation sweep: remember when you started the last walk and send it as `since`. `status` and `type` take one value or a comma list (`status=pending,scheduled`). Organization-scoped, authorised by the executor key (or a partner link with `privacy:execute`), like every executor route.

From `Forumulate-Version: 2027-01-01` this list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), leaves the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) out of each row unless `include` names them, and keeps only the `fields` you list. Earlier versions are unchanged. See /reference/versioning.

put.description:
Reads one document describing what this organization should have — spaces, their theme, redirects, collections, forum categories, status monitors, and org-level AI knowledge sources — and reports a per-unit DIFF against what is there today. **Nothing is written unless you send `?apply=true`.** Idempotent: applying the same manifest twice does the work once, and the second run answers `unchanged` for every unit. Additive: anything present that the manifest does not declare is reported under `extras` and never deleted. Each block is validated by the schema of the endpoint that owns it, so the manifest accepts exactly what those endpoints accept, and each unit re-checks that endpoint’s own capability — a dry run is refused wherever the apply would be. An apply is NOT one transaction (each subsystem opens its own, which is where tenant isolation lives); it is a sequence of idempotent units that stops at the first failure and names where it stopped, so a partial apply is resumed by fixing the manifest and applying again. The vocabulary for `type`, and which blocks a given type may declare, come from `GET /space-types`. **Version 2** (`"version": 2`, FMU-X07) adds the provisioning units `domains`, `reader_auth`, `consent`, `connectors`, `executor`, `webhooks`, `status_monitors` and `brand`, all naming spaces and sites by slug. Each goes through the generic registry its own endpoint uses — any IdP, any CMP, any connector provider. The answer adds `steps` — on a dry run `{unit, ref, action: create|update|unchanged|delete|unsupported, diff, requires, id}`, on an apply `{unit, ref, id, action, status, readBack: ok|mismatch}` with a read-back after every write — plus `manual: [{kind: "dns", name, type, value}, …]` for what only the customer can do, and `job` (the apply as a job). Re-running after a kill creates no duplicates: each unit’s resource is ledgered as it lands, and found by its natural key when the ledger missed it. Secrets minted by a step (a webhook signing secret, an executor key) are in that step’s `shownOnce`, in this answer only; send `X-Secret-Recipient` to seal them. Every `status_monitors` (or version-1 `monitors`) apply step for a heartbeat monitor — created, updated or unchanged — carries its `pingUrl` — the URL the job POSTs to, also on `GET /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/status/monitors`; it is in this answer only, never in the stored run. A `domains` step whose declared `state` waits on a proof not served yet carries `waiting` (what each proof method saw: file answered 404, wrong contents, no TXT) — on the plan before anything is written, and on the apply, where under `onUnverified: hold` (the default) the domain stays claimed, the step is `applied` and the run carries on. `prune: true` deletes what the manifest itself created and no longer declares. `brand` answers `unsupported` where no brand service is installed. **Publisher blocks** (version 2, DX-D) make one document cover a whole content-as-code publisher: on each `spaces[]` entry `locales`, `seo` (merged per key), `translations` (per language: name, description, `seoTitle`, `seoDescription`, generated pages), `preset`/`piecePreset`/`frontDoor`, a CONTACT space’s `contactForm` (with `translations.<code>.nextSteps`) and an ABOUT space’s `about`; a top-level `pages` list (Markdown `body` or `sections`, `title`, `seoTitle`, `seoDescription`, `canonicalUrl`, `metadata`, `collection`, `order`, and `translations.<code>` twins); and `sites` (config — chrome, theme, `headerLinks`, `searchSettings`, `search` — merged or, with `configMode: replace`, replaced, plus member `spaces` by slug). Every one is written through its own door and read back; a page edited outside the manifest since the last apply is reported as drift in `diff.content`. Under `prune: true` only the kinds the document declares are pruned (pages go to the trash). `forumulate plan` / `forumulate apply` build this document from a `forumulate.yaml` and a Markdown folder.

**Requires token scope: `write`** — see "Token scopes" under Authentication.

parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or its `slug`. One you are not a member of is a 404.

parameters.name: apply
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

parameters.name: X-Secret-Recipient
parameters.description: `x25519:<base64 32-byte public key>`. When sent, every shown-once secret in the answer is null and sealed instead (a libsodium sealed box only the matching private key opens). A malformed key is a 422 and nothing is minted.
