info.title: Forumulate API
info.description:
The full Forumulate REST API — identity, organizations, spaces, docs authoring, publishing, search, AI, webhooks, and the public reader. Authenticate with a Personal Access Token (Bearer) or the session cookie. Download this spec at `/api/openapi.json` (YAML at `/api/openapi.yaml`) to generate a client SDK (e.g. with openapi-generator).

**Set your own `User-Agent`.** `/api/*` accepts any User-Agent, library defaults included. `/api/auth/*` is bot-protected at the edge: some library defaults (`Python-urllib` among them) get a Cloudflare **403** whose body is `error code: 1010`, an HTML/plain-text page rather than a JSON error. Any identifying string (e.g. `my-app-integration/1.0`) passes.

## Conventions

**One rule for identifiers: a uuid or a slug, and the answer carries the uuid.**
Every `{orgId}` and `{spaceId}` accepts either the uuid or the name in
`slug`; so do `{siteId}` and `{libraryId}` within their organization, and
`{pageId}`, `{collectionId}` and `{categoryId}` within their space. Such a
parameter points at the `IdOrSlug` component; every other id says "UUID only".
A name that is not yours is a 404 naming the parameter (`error.param`), never a
500 and never a 400. `GET /resolve?org=&space=&page=` turns names into ids and
public URLs in one call.

**Every response is in this document — read the key, never guess it.** Each
operation now publishes its response schema, derived from the handler's own
return type, so the key that holds a list is stated rather than inferred.
Two rules explain the names you will see:

* An ORGANIZATION-level collection is keyed after its path: `/spaces` answers
  `{ spaces }`, `/webhooks` answers `{ webhooks }`, `/orgs` answers
  `{ orgs }` — and `{ organizations }` too, which is what it has always
  answered.
* A SPACE's content is keyed by that space type's own word for a piece, not by
  the path. `GET …/blog` answers `{ articles }`, `…/forum` answers
  `{ topics }`, `…/changelog` answers `{ releases }`, `…/roadmap` answers
  `{ items }`, `…/collections` answers `{ collections }`. The vocabulary is
  published as data at `GET /space-types` (`vocabulary.piece`,
  `vocabulary.container`), so the key for a type you have not integrated yet
  is one request away. Guessing `topics` for a blog has cost one integrator a
  duplicate article; the schema on the operation is the answer.

**Send `Forumulate-Version: 2027-03-01` on every request.** It is the newest
version and includes every one before it. `2026-09-01` is the paging envelope;
`2026-11-01` drops the snake_case `has_more`/`next_cursor`; `2026-12-01`
refuses unknown body fields with a 422, answers a taken page slug with 409
unless you send `onSlugTaken: "suffix"`, and joins a new public space to a
site only when you send `siteId`; `2027-01-01` answers lean lists (rows once,
under `data`, bodies only on `?include=`), one `status` on topic rows, the
shared job object alone, and requires `?confirm=` on the deprecated purge names.
A version, once served, never changes: a caller pinned to `2026-11-01` keeps
exactly what it had. The header is
optional only so that integrations written before versioning keep working.

**State your version and you get the envelope.** Send
`Forumulate-Version: 2026-09-01` or later and the ENVELOPED collections carry `page`
(`limit`, `hasMore`, `nextCursor`, `total`) **and `data`** — the same rows as
the named key, so one parser reads every collection (a blog's `articles` are
also under `topics`, the forum's word for the same objects); walks also carry
`sync.checkpoint`. Send nothing and you get the pre-envelope shape, plus
`Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on THOSE operations saying so. Everywhere
else the header is accepted and changes nothing, and no removal date is sent —
the operations are not deprecated, only the shape they negotiate.

It is universal, and universal is checked rather than claimed: 448 GETs publish a `limit` over rows, and every one
of them but the 24 rankings below takes `cursor` and carries `page` for a caller who states a version. That
holds for the 411 whose whole answer IS a collection and for every answer that merely CONTAINS a
collection: a surface's front page (`…/blog`, `…/forum`, `…/roadmap`) pages
the rows it wraps in chrome, and a log that comes with a summary beside it
(`…/api-activity`) pages the log. Three walks over the published document
assert it (`openapi-list-paging.test.ts`): no list without `limit`, no list
without `page`, and nothing that publishes `limit` over rows and then answers
no `page` — so an endpoint added after this sentence is covered by being one.

The 24 exceptions are RANKINGS rather than collections — the reputation
leaderboards, every `?q=` search (unified, semantic, per-space), recent
search terms, the search-gap and uncovered-thread reports, and a topic's
related topics — where a score is recomputed per request and so there is no row
a cursor could resume after; they honour `limit` per item, and each one now
carries its own reason on its own answer, in prose and as
`x-forumulate-no-paging`, so you need not come back here to find out why.
Four of them are not rankings but the changelog FEED documents
(`…/changelog.json`, `…/changelog.xml`), which page by their own standard — JSON Feed's
`next_url`, Atom's `rel="next"` — so feed readers can walk them.

`limit` counts the thing you came for. On a GROUPED answer that is not the
groups: the roadmap board's lanes are the status columns it shows, so
`?limit=1` gives you one ITEM in each lane rather than one lane, and a cursor
goes one page deeper in every lane at once.

Every number in this paragraph is counted off the finished document rather than
typed here — a hand tally beside a generated contract drifts by construction,
which is how this page came to claim "9 of 295" while the document said
otherwise.

A route whose two answers really differ answers BOTH shapes and lets you
choose: the pre-envelope body to a caller who states no version, the envelope to
one who does. Every such operation declares the two as an `anyOf` of exactly
two variants — the withdrawn one marked `deprecated` with its removal date,
the other listing `page` as required — and sends `Deprecation`/`Sunset`
only on those. So the set is two lines of the document rather than a list in
this paragraph, which is what it used to be and which was wrong: a shape served
only to unversioned callers used to be published as one object with an optional
`page`, and an optional field cannot be told apart from one that is merely
sometimes absent, nor carry a date. The two are never mixed in one response, so
`page` has exactly one type per answer. Each operation's published response
schema says which it is — that, and not this paragraph, is the thing to code
against.

`page` also carries `has_more` and `next_cursor`, the same two values under
their original spellings. They were the only snake_case keys in an otherwise
camelCase document, which is an inconsistency three integrators reported. They
are deprecated, and deprecated here means dated rather than permanent: state
`2026-11-01` or later and the envelope arrives without them. `2026-09-01` and
the unversioned shape keep them for as long as the policy above says, so there
is nothing to migrate in a hurry — read `hasMore` and `nextCursor`, which are
sent on every version.

`2026-12-01` changes one default: an unset
`onSlugTaken` on `POST …/collections/{collectionId}/pages` and
`PATCH …/pages/{pageId}` means `fail` (409) instead of `suffix`, so a page
never lands at an address nobody wrote unless you ask for that. Earlier versions,
and no version, keep `suffix`.

A cursor names a row, never an offset, so a walk cannot skip or repeat one when
the set changes under it. Two listings are ranked rather than ordered — the
forum index under `?sort=top` and any listing with `?q=` — and a place in a
ranking is not a place: those answer `nextCursor: null` and continue with
`?page=`.

Four aggregate listings are the stated exception, and the exception is stated
rather than hidden: `/assets`, both member directories and the community tag
feed rank by an aggregate that moves as its window slides, so there is no row a
walk could resume after. Their `nextCursor` is an opaque token carrying the
next PAGE, and it inherits exactly the hazard `?page=` always had there — a
row written mid-walk can shift the set, so one may repeat or be missed at a
page boundary. It is opaque on purpose: when one of them grows an ordering a
cursor can name, it changes underneath you and your code does not.

**A create answers 201, and the envelope is `{ <resource>, data }`.** This is
the one create shape; there is no second one to learn.

    HTTP/1.1 201 Created

    {
      "page": { "id": "…", "title": "…", … },
      "data": { "id": "…", "title": "…", … }
    }

`data` is the KEY TO READ if you are writing one client for many endpoints: it
is on every create that makes a single thing, and it holds the created
resource. The other key — `page`, `article`, `topic`, `pat`,
`webhook`, named after what the collection calls a member — is the canonical
name, is what the operation's schema documents, and is the one to read if you
are integrating one endpoint. They are the SAME object, not a copy: nothing is
renamed, nothing is removed, and a client reading `response.page` is
unaffected. `GET /space-types` publishes the per-type vocabulary if you want
to know a key before you call.

Read `data ?? <the named key>` and you have covered every create, including
the 85 of 283 that answer 201 with no
`data` — because a 201 is not a promise that something addressable was made.
Those are a **result** (an acknowledgement, a computed answer, a tally, a
one-time credential), a
**collection** (the whole list you added to, with no single row to point at) or
a **bare resource** (the resource itself at the top level, with no key beside it
to hang a mirror on). Each one SAYS which it is in its own 201 description, so
you never have to infer it from the shape.

A create may carry more beside those two, and none of it is the resource:
`ok`, `warnings` (a value we accepted and rewrote), `conformance` (a piece
against its shape), `slugChanged` (`{ asked, used }`), and the one-time
secret a credential mint shows you once — `POST /pats` answers
`{ token, pat, data }`, where `token` is the secret and `pat`/`data` are
the row. So: read `data` for the thing that was made, and read the named
siblings for what we did while making it.

**Some creates answer no single resource, on purpose, and have no `data`.**
They are not an oversight, and each one states its own kind on its own 201 — so
the set is read off this document rather than counted here, where a number
would be stale the first time one of them is keyed (two were):

* an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT — `{ ok: true }` from a flag, a subscribe, a consent
  receipt. Nothing was addressed, so there is nothing to return.
* the WHOLE COLLECTION — `POST …/docs/locales` answers every locale, not the
  one you added. `data` meaning "the thing that was made" on
  198 routes and "all of them" on 14 is
  worse for a generic client than `data` being absent on those
  14.
* a RESULT with no address — an RPC, a search, a quiz attempt, a share-link
  mint (`{ id, token }`), an `archive-to-topic`. There is no row to GET
  back, so there is no resource to mirror.
* TWO resources — `POST …/groups/{groupId}/message` makes a channel and a
  message. Picking one of them to be `data` would be a guess.
* the resource ITSELF, unkeyed — SCIM `POST /scim/v2/Users` and `/Groups`,
  because RFC 7644 defines the response as the resource and a `data` key there
  would make us non-conformant with the spec your IdP implements. These two are
  the only ones left: `POST …/events` and
  `POST …/change-requests/{crId}/comments` were listed here as breaking
  changes waiting for a dated version, and when the callers that reason named
  were checked for, there were none — both answer `{ <resource>, data }` now.

A POST that answers **200** at a collection address is doing something else
again: an upsert (one row per subject, re-sent freely), a toggle, or an RPC.

**`content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES, not a field and a fallback.**
Everything with a body of prose — a forum topic, a blog post, a changelog
release, a roadmap item, and every reply and comment on them — takes it as block
JSON in `content` or as Markdown in `markdown`, converted server-side into
the same blocks. Send ONE. Sending both is a 422 naming `markdown`: nothing
silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise get a
201 and the wrong body. Each of those request bodies is published as a
`oneOf` of the two forms for exactly that reason — it used to be one object
with `content` required and `markdown` optional, which refused a body this
API accepts and permitted one it refuses.

**A named layout is validated against its type's list, which is published.**
`PUT /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/preset` takes a `preset` (and sometimes a
`piecePreset`) whose valid values depend on the SPACE's type, so no single
enum on the operation can be right. The list, with a sentence describing each
layout, is at `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` — and the whole vocabulary at
`GET /space-types`. The operation's description enumerates every type's
layouts too, so you can read it without a second request.

**A colour has one spelling per surface, and both are stated.** A THEME token
(`theme.colors.*`) is a six-digit hex with the leading `#` and nothing
else; a bare `0b835b` is a 422 that says so. A COMMUNITY colour — a forum
category, a tag, group flair — is wider, because it ends up in a style
attribute: hex with or without the `#` (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits) or a CSS colour
name, normalised on the way in to the canonical form. `0b835b` is therefore
accepted there and stored as `#0b835b`; it used to be stored exactly as sent,
which is not a colour any browser draws, so the coloured border the guide
promises was simply never there.

**A boolean query parameter is `true`/`false`.** `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`
and `on`/`off` are accepted as well. What is NOT accepted is a value that
looks boolean and is read as something else: `?unhandled=true` once reached a
route that tested for the literal string `1`, so it filtered nothing and
answered 200 with the opposite of what was asked for. Any other value is a 422
naming the parameter.

**`If-Match` is evaluated where it can be, and refused where it cannot.**

Two resources have it, and they have it on EVERY write: a **page** and an
**item**. The tag is the `ETag` on the read — opaque, and it changes on ANY
change to the representation (body, title, slug, `locale`, metadata), so it
is right for `If-None-Match` as well. It is computed by the same function the
write checks against, so a tag we just issued is never refused. `contentHash`
in the body still changes only on content and is still accepted as `If-Match`,
guarding the content only. Send it as `If-Match` on any write to that resource —
its body, a single slot, its metadata, its slug, its shape, its order, a
publish, an unpublish, a rollback, a schedule, a duplicate, a restore, a
verify, a delete, a purge — and a resource that has moved on answers `412`,
naming both the hash you sent and the one it is at. Re-read and retry.

It took three passes to be able to write that sentence. First only
`PUT …/pages/{pageId}/content` evaluated the header; then the page's own
`PATCH` still answered `428`, so the slug and the metadata — the fields two
people in a console actually race on — had no control at all; then
`PUT …/pages/{pageId}/sections/{key}`, which loads a whole document and swaps
one slot, was still unconditional while its twin on an item was not. A
precondition that holds on some of a resource's doors is one a client cannot
build on, which is why this is now stated as "every write" rather than as a
list of routes.

A write that carries a concrete `If-Match` and CANNOT evaluate it is refused
with `428`; `If-Match: *` passes through, since it only asserts the resource
exists. This is deliberate: the header used to be IGNORED, so a caller who sent
it believed they had optimistic concurrency and lost the write in the exact case
the header exists to catch. What is left on 428 is only what one tag could not
be about — `bulk-delete`, `bulk-move` and `empty-trash`, which address a
selection rather than a resource, and a create, which has no prior state
(`Idempotency-Key` is what makes a create safe to retry). Where another
resource has real concurrency control it is explicit and named — a docs change
request, a theme draft (`theme_draft.stale`, publish with `force`).

**Nothing is dropped in silence.** State `Forumulate-Version: 2026-12-01` (or
later) and ONE rule holds on every write: a request-body field the operation
does not recognise — at the top level or inside a block document — is a 422
naming its path, and nothing is written. On an earlier version, or none, such a
field is dropped and reported on `X-Unrecognized-Fields` (the 200 still
stands), except on the routes below, which always refuse. The THEME routes
(`PUT|PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/theme` and
`PUT …/reader-themes`) always refuse: a 422 naming the key and its path, e.g.
`chrome.footerColumns.0.title`. A theme key we ignore has no other symptom —
the write answers 200, the read-back echoes what you sent, and only the page
looks wrong — so there is nothing to notice unless we say so. A field we
ACCEPTED but rewrote — a slugified tag,
a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken — is reported on
`X-Field-Warnings` as `field: what we did`, **and in the answer itself as
`warnings[]`**, on every write whose answer is a JSON object. That second
channel is the one that matters to code: the header shipped first and was the
only channel on 77 of the 89 writes that can rewrite something, so a client
that parses JSON — which is all of them — saw a 2xx and nothing else. It is
absent when nothing was rewritten, never `[]`. A value we KEPT that this space's type never
renders (`seo.pages.blog.tag` on a forum) is named the same way. A key whose
meaning MOVED says where it went — "X is now …; use Y (since …; docs: …)" — in a
422's `details` and `hint`, or on `X-Field-Warnings` when the old spelling
is still accepted or was dropped. Both headers are exposed
through CORS. If you get a
2xx and either header is present, the stored value is not the value you sent.

**One code, one status.** The code is the only part of an error to branch on, so
it says what KIND of failure this is — and it appears on exactly one status, so
you never have to read both. `request.malformed` is the 400: the request could
not be understood or was incomplete (a malformed header, an unparseable path
value, a multipart upload with no file part, a body that is not valid UTF-8).
`validation.failed` is the 422
and nothing else: it was understood and a value is unacceptable. That is the
ordinary one and it carries `details`, keyed by field path. `payload.too_large`
is the 413 (split it), `media.unsupported` the 415 (convert it),
`gone` the 410 (it existed and has been withdrawn — stop asking) and
`precondition.failed` the 412 (re-read and retry); each of those four used to
be `validation.failed` as well, which is how one code came to mean nine
different things. `not_found` is the 404 (a namespaced
`org.not_found`/`space.not_found`/`pat.not_found`/`member.not_found`
only where you must act differently). `conflict` is the 409 over the
resource's STATE — an id taken, a channel closed, a queue item another
moderator claimed. `service_unavailable` is a dependency failing, including a
502/504 from an upstream we called for you: retryable, and it carries
`Retry-After`. `internal` means we have a bug and retrying will not help.
A feature that needs a credential nobody has supplied (`ai.unavailable`,
`atlas.not_configured`) is a **409**, never a 503 — a 503 carries
`Retry-After`, and there is nothing to wait for.

**An error names the field, the allowed values and where to read more.** The
envelope is `{ error: { code, message, details }, requestId }`, where
`details` is keyed by field path. A 422 over a controlled vocabulary lists that
vocabulary in the message (`One of: standard, no-front-door.`) and
`error.docs` links the reference page for the endpoint. `requestId` is the
same value as the `x-request-id` header, repeated in the body because that is
the half of a failure that reaches a bug report — quote it and we can find your
exact request.

**Rate limits are per minute.** Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`,
`RateLimit-Policy` (`600;w=60` — the limit and the window in seconds),
`RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`. A 429 also carries
`Retry-After`.

**A chat/AI connector authenticates as itself.** A connector token
(`Authorization: Bearer fmwc_…`) identifies one connector bound to one
space, so the `/connector/kb/*` endpoints take no `orgId` or `spaceId`
in the path — the token already says which. `GET /connector/kb/manifest`
describes every other endpoint, the capabilities that token actually holds, and
the chunk policy version. This replaces passing a `source` string in a request
body: an author a caller can choose is not an author.

**Removals are discoverable for 30 days.** `include_deleted=true` carries
tombstones, so an incremental sync never has to fall back to a full list to
learn what went away.

**Slots carry roles, and the vocabulary is published.** `GET /roles` returns
the controlled list, each role's canonical reading position and a gloss, plus
what an unroled slot does. It is versioned: a new role is a version bump, not a
silent change to how your articles order themselves.

**Chunks are ours to split.** `GET /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/items/{itemId}/chunks`
returns retrieval-grade chunks with a per-chunk `contentHash`, so you
re-embed what changed rather than everything. The split is a contract once you
store a `chunkId`: `policy.version` changing is a breaking change.

A **chunk's** `contentHash` is a 28-character base36 digest with no prefix —
compare it with the one you stored, and nothing else. It is deliberately not a
cryptographic hash: the splitter runs in the browser too. Everywhere else in
this API — a page, an item — `contentHash` is `sha256:<64 hex>`, which you
may also compare by hand. The two shapes are not comparable with each other,
and neither is comparable across resources: a page hashes its canonicalised
block document, an item the markdown it renders to.

**A webhook signature is a LIST, and you check for membership.**
`X-Forumulate-Signature` carries every signature a delivery has, comma
separated:

    v1,sha256=<hex>, v1,sha256=<hex>, sha256=<hex>, sha256=<hex>

`v1` is HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}` and is the one to
verify — the timestamp is inside the signed base, which is what stops a
captured delivery being replayed. A bare `sha256=` is the legacy body-only
signature; it is replayable by construction and rides along until an endpoint's
`signatureVersion` is set to `v1`. There is one entry per live secret, so a
rotation puts two of each in the header and both verify.

**The body-only `sha256=` entry stops being sent on 2027-10-05.**
It was described as "being retired" with no date, which is not something a
receiver can plan around. After that day a delivery carries `v1` entries
only; `v1` itself does not change, and an endpoint already set to
`signatureVersion: v1` has not been sent a `v0` entry since it was set. If
you check that the header CONTAINS your computed `v1` value, as above, the
date passes without you doing anything.

This paragraph used to describe a single signature, which invited
`header === expected` — and every delivery to an endpoint on the default
`both`, and every delivery during a rotation, then failed to verify. Compute
your `v1` value and check that the header CONTAINS it. There is a tested
implementation in `@forumulate/sdk` — `verifyWebhookSignature`, which
takes the raw body and both headers and returns a boolean:

    const ok = await verifyWebhookSignature({
      secret,
      body: rawBody,   // the RAW bytes. A re-serialised body never verifies.
      signature: headers['x-forumulate-signature'],
      timestamp: headers['x-forumulate-timestamp'],
    });

It checks membership rather than equality, and it rejects a delivery older
than five minutes, which is what the signed timestamp is for.

Also on every delivery: `X-Forumulate-Timestamp`, `X-Forumulate-Event` and
`X-Forumulate-Delivery` (the key to dedupe on — a retry reuses it).
`GET /orgs/{orgId}/webhooks/events` says which event means which change.


## Authentication

### Token scopes

Every authenticated operation names its **token scope** — `read`, `write` or `admin`, the coarse method gate — for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth. It applies *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs: the coarse scope gates the HTTP method, a catalog scope (`docs:read`, `webhooks:manage`, …) narrows which resources the token may touch, and a token needs both. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead. An operation that takes no credential names no scope.

pat.description: Atlas API key (`ak_…`, what **Account → Tokens** issues for an Atlas-linked account), Personal Access Token (`cft_…`, the local fallback), OAuth access token (`cfo_…`) or connector token (`fmwc_…`). Opaque strings — there is nothing inside one to parse.

delivery_key.description: Content delivery key, issued under a content library’s Keys: `cfd_…` (server-side, published content), `cfp_…` (publishable, answers only its listed browser origins) or `cfv_…` (preview, drafts). Accepted only by `/delivery/*`; every other route refuses one.

cookie.name: forumulate_session
cookie.description: The browser session cookie, set by signing in and sent automatically by the browser. OpenAPI calls every cookie credential an "apiKey" because that is the only type it has for one — this is NOT an API key: you cannot mint it, copy it into a header, or use it from a server. For that, hold a token (`Authorization: Bearer ak_…` / `cft_…`). Cookie calls are governed by RBAC capabilities rather than by token scopes.

name.description: What this token is for, so a list of them is readable a year later.

scopes.description: The coarse HTTP gate: `read` to read, `write` to author, `admin` to issue further tokens. Required. A catalog name (`docs:read`) sent here is accepted and MOVED to `scopeGrants`, so reading the token back shows only the gate it derived — not what you sent. **Recommended form:** `scopes` (the coarse read/write/admin gate) + `capabilities` (exactly what the token may do, from the capability enum) + `constraints` (exactly where: org, space and category ids). A request outside either answers 403. `scopeGrants` (catalog names that expand into capabilities) and the top-level `spaceIds` (the same thing as `constraints.spaceIds`) are LEGACY: still honoured, no removal date, but new integrations should not need them.

expiresInDays.description: Expire it after this many days: 1–365. Omit for 90. Every new key expires within a year (`null`, never, is refused); tokens minted earlier keep their expiry.

spaceIds.description: LEGACY — use `constraints.spaceIds`, which means the same and sits with the other resource pins. Still honoured, no removal date. The spaces this token may touch; omit for everywhere its owner can go.

capabilities.description: RECOMMENDED. Exactly the capabilities this token may exercise (e.g. `docs.write`, `org.manage_members`), for least privilege. Omit for a token that carries the whole of its owner’s reach. Enforced on top of the scope and the owner’s grants — the token is their intersection — and stored exactly as sent, so the read-back matches.

scopeGrants.description: LEGACY — name `capabilities` directly. Still honoured, no removal date. Named scopes from the published catalog (`GET /pats/scopes`), e.g. `docs:read`; each EXPANDS into a bundle of capabilities, and the union is what is stored and enforced as `capabilities`.

constraints.description: RECOMMENDED. Pin the token to specific org/space/category ids. A request targeting a resource outside the set is denied (403) even when the scope and the owner’s grants would allow it. Omit for an unconstrained token.

externalRef.description: Your own name for this token. Get-or-create: a live token of yours already holding it answers 200 with `idempotent: true` and `secret: null` (a secret is shown once) — rotate it to get a new secret.

metadata.description: Flat key → value labels, filterable on the list as `?metadata[key]=value`.

scopes.description: The coarse gate only (read/write/admin). Catalog names sent in `scopes` on create are stored as `scopeGrants`, so this is not necessarily what you sent — `capabilities` and `constraints` are what the token is actually limited by.

lastUsedAt.description: When it was last used to make a request.

spaceIds.description: The spaces it is confined to, when it is.

capabilities.description: The capabilities it is narrowed to, when it is.

scopeGrants.description: The named catalog scopes this token was created with (`docs:read`, …), or null if it named none. Descriptive: `capabilities` above is what is enforced, so re-pointing a scope name at a different bundle can never widen a token that already exists.

applicationName.description: The app holding this key, when it is a device key.

secret.description: The secret — the same string as the top-level `token`, on the object you are likely to keep. Present on this answer ONLY: every later read of the token is a summary, because the secret is stored hashed. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.

token.description: The secret. Shown once, on this response, and never again — also on `pat.secret` (and `data.secret`). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

pat.description: The token row, with `secret` on it. `data` is the same object.

applicationName.description: The app holding this key, when it is a device key.

limit.description: The limit this page was built with — what was asked for, capped. It is NOT the number of rows returned: a final page under the limit is normal, and `has_more` is the only thing that says whether to keep walking.

hasMore.description: Whether another page follows this one.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to continue. Null on the last page.

has_more.description: The same value as `hasMore`. The only snake_case keys in this API are these two. Sent to callers who state `2026-09-01` or no version at all; ABSENT from `2026-11-01` onwards. Read `hasMore` instead — it is sent on every version.

next_cursor.description: The same value as `nextCursor`. Absent from `2026-11-01` onwards; read `nextCursor`.

total.description: Rows in the whole collection — the size of the set, not of this page, and not of what you have seen so far. ABSENT where the source cannot count the collection: the append-only logs (staff actions, automation runs, connector activity, ingested questions, chat history) grow without bound and are not counted on every page view. Walk on `hasMore`, which is exact on every answer; read `total` only to show a size, and handle its absence.

page.description: Present once a caller states a version.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

PatListDto.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

description.description: What granting this scope lets a token do.

order.description: Canonical reading position. Lower comes first.

gloss.description: What belongs in a slot of this role, in one line.

version.description: The API version this vocabulary belongs to. A new role is a version bump.

unroledPolicy.description: What to do with a slot carrying no role. `inherit-previous`: it takes the rank of the last roled slot before it, so a verification step stays with the steps it verifies instead of drifting to the end. A slot before the FIRST roled one inherits `summary` (rank 0).

slotKeys.description: A slot KEY is not a role. Roles are this closed, global, six-word vocabulary; keys come from a space’s shape, differ by space type and preset, and an owner may add or omit one. A slot may declare a role and most do not — an unroled slot ranks as `unroledPolicy` says, which means a role filter that ignores the policy silently drops most of a page. The declared key→role mapping for every type and preset is published at `GET /space-types/slots`; one space’s own slots are at `GET /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/shape`.

slug.description: The first segment of every public address this organization owns.

slug.description: The segment this space answers to on a site.

itemCount.description: How many pieces are in it, so a picker can warn before an import.

itemsUpdatedAt.description: When anything in this space last changed, or null for an empty space. `itemCount` says how big a space is; this says whether it is worth walking. Compare it to the value you stored last sync and skip the space entirely when it has not moved.

url.description: Where this space is published — the customer's own domain when they have one, ours otherwise. Null when the space is not public.

siteId.description: The site this space is published on (one of `GET /orgs/{orgId}/sites`), or null when it is on none. When several sites name the space, the oldest. Set it with `siteId` on create, or by naming the space in a site's `spaceIds`.

data.description: Mirrors `space` — the uniform create envelope.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices about the space just created — e.g. the slug collides with a reserved platform path, so the space is unreachable on our hostname though fine on a custom domain. Absent when there is nothing to warn about.

page.description: Present once a caller states a version.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

tag.description: A meta tag to place on the domain’s home page as proof of ownership.

name.description: The record name to create (the hostname).

value.description: The record value — our edge host (CNAME) or IP (A).

basePath.description: The path this domain publishes under, or '' for the whole hostname.

active.description: True once we ANSWER this address. Separate from `verified`: `POST {domainId}/verify {"activate": false}` proves ownership without switching traffic, so your own application keeps serving the path until `POST {domainId}/activate`.

verifiedAt.description: When ownership was proven; null while `verified` is false.

activatedAt.description: When we started answering this address; null while `active` is false.

alsoRedirectWww.description: Also answer `www.<hostname>` (same path) with a permanent redirect to this address, written into our proxy. Default false: a domain is registered for ONE hostname, so without it `www.acme.com/docs` reaches whatever else answers that name (often your own app, which 404s). Leave it off when your own app already redirects www; `GET …/setup` reports `wwwNotCovered` either way. Refused (422) on a hostname that already starts with `www.`. Point the www name’s DNS where the bare name points; for a whole-host domain we also request its certificate.

ipAllowList.description: The networks (addresses and CIDR blocks) that may read this address; `[]` means anywhere. Set with `PUT {domainId}/ip-allow-list`.

redirectTo.description: When set, every request on this address answers 301 to this URL plus its path; null while it serves. Set with `PUT {domainId}/redirect`.

verificationRecord.description: The TXT record that proves ownership.

verificationFile.description: A file to place on the site as an alternative ownership proof.

dnsTarget.description: The DNS record to create so traffic reaches us (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex); null when the deployment configures no target.

settling.description: True only on the answer of a call that just took the address live (`activate`, or `verify` with `activate`): routing settles within about 60 seconds, and a `setup` read before then may say pending or "answered 308" — that is not a failure. Absent on reads.
Mirrors `domain.settling`: true when this call just took the address live and routing is still settling (about 60 s).

found.description: The A records the hostname currently resolves to.

expected.description: An edge address we accept, when the deployment pins one.

reachesUs.description: True once the hostname resolves to (or CNAMEs to) our edge.

cnameTarget.description: The CNAME target the hostname points at, when it is a CNAME.

resolves.description: The twin resolves in DNS at all.

covered.description: Readers who type the twin end up at this address.

how.description: How it is covered: 'redirect-by-us' (alsoRedirectWww is on), 'registered' (the twin is a live address of its own here), 'redirects-here' (something — usually your app — already redirects it to this address), 'served-by-us' (it already reaches our edge); or why not: 'not-resolving' (no DNS record, nothing to cover), 'not-covered' (it resolves and something else answers).

detail.description: One sentence a person can act on.

url.description: The reader root at this address.

active.description: Whether this address is served yet. `false` is a claimed custom domain that is not verified or not switched on: its URLs work once it goes live, so a hand-off can be shipped before cut-over.

jwtRedeemUrl.description: Redeem an external_jwt here (`POST {jwt, returnTo}` or `GET ?jwt=…&returnTo=…`) so the reader cookies are set on THIS host. Redeeming on forumulate.com sets them there, where your docs never see them.

signOutUrl.description: `POST` here to revoke the reader session and clear every reader cookie on this host. Or navigate the browser to it as a link — `GET ?orgId=…&spaceId=…&returnTo=…` — from your product's own sign-out: same effect, then a 302 to `returnTo` (the space, or your sign-in/sign-out page's origin).

path.description: The path prefix to forward to us.

origin.description: The edge origin the proxy must target (origin.forumulate.com), NOT the marketing apex.

mode.description: Which configuration step this domain is on: 'verified' = already reaching our edge (nothing to do); 'dns' = a whole host that must point at us; 'pending' = we are not answering this address yet, either because it is verified but NOT ACTIVATED (your own application still serves it — call `POST {domainId}/activate` when ready) or because it was activated moments ago and routing is still settling; 'path' = an ACTIVATED subfolder that still does not reach us and needs one proxy rule; 'unverified' = a subfolder not verified yet. Only 'path' means "add a proxy rule" — read `message` for which case `pending` is.

pendingReason.description: Which `pending` this is, so a caller can branch without reading `message` (null on every other mode): 'not_activated' = verified but not activated (a whole host already points at us) — call `POST {domainId}/activate` when ready; 'not_resolving' = a whole host verified but not activated whose DNS does not reach our edge yet — point it at us, then activate; 'shadowed' = a path that reaches our edge while a shorter live mount of the same host answers it — verify and activate it (or wait if it was just activated); 'settling' = activated within the last 15 minutes and not visibly serving yet — re-check in a minute, build nothing; 'unchecked' = our probe could not reach the address (timeout, connection error or a 5xx), so this answer says nothing either way — `servedState` is `unknown`; re-check shortly, build nothing.

served.description: True when traffic already reaches our edge and the domain is serving now.

servedState.description: Three-valued `served`: 'yes' = proven serving now; 'no' = our probe got an answer and it was not this mount's; 'unknown' = the probe itself failed (timeout, connection error, 5xx) — `served` is then false but means "could not check", not "not served".

checkedAt.description: When this answer was checked (the probe runs on every call; nothing is cached).

crawlerBlocked.description: True when a CDN in front of the domain blocks crawler/AI User-Agents, so the (public) docs are invisible to search engines and AI tools until the owner allows bot traffic.

message.description: A one-line, human-readable summary of what to do next (or that nothing is needed).

wwwNotCovered.description: True when `www.<hostname>` resolves in DNS but does NOT reach this address — readers who type www land on whatever else answers that name. Fix it with `alsoRedirectWww`, or a redirect in your own app. Absent for a hostname that already starts with `www.`.

www.description: What we found at the `www.` twin of this hostname, and how it is covered.

readerEndpoints.description: The same-origin reader-session endpoints at this address (space domains only — a site domain's are per space, on `GET …/spaces/{spaceId}/reader-auth` → `readerEndpoints`).

forward.description: The single reverse-proxy rule to add, when a path-based domain does not yet reach us.

source.description: The integration that reported this standing (e.g. "my-app").

label.description: What this standing is called on the source platform.

value.description: The rank value. Null when the source tracks a tier but no number.

tier.description: A named tier, when the source has one.

profileUrl.description: Link to the member's profile on the source.

iconUrl.description: Icon for the standing, when the source supplies one.

updatedAt.description: When this standing was last pushed.

leaders.description: Members ranked by the source’s value, highest first. The key is `leaders`.

verifiedAt.description: When somebody last said this is still correct. Null means nobody ever has.

ageDays.description: Days since that, or since it last changed when it has never been verified.

stale.description: Whether that exceeds the space's staleness policy.

confidence.description: How much to trust it, 0 to 1. A number rather than a flag because it is meant to be multiplied into your own ranking: recent content should outrank old content without the old disappearing.

id.description: The piece's own id, the same value its kind's own routes use — so `/items` joins to them on `id`. A `page` item's id IS the page id: the `id` of the matching `PageListRow` from `GET /orgs/{orgId}/spaces/{spaceId}/pages`, and the `{pageId}` of every `…/pages/{pageId}` route (a language twin is its own page, with its own id, in both lists). A `topic` item's id is the topic id the blog, forum, changelog and roadmap routes take (`…/blog/{topicId}`, `…/forum/{topicId}`); topics are not in `…/pages`. An `incident` item's id is the `{incidentId}` of `…/status/incidents/{incidentId}`.

kind.description: What backs this piece in storage.

slug.description: The name this piece answers to in an address.

published.description: Whether a reader with no account can see it.

group.description: The collection a page sits in, where the space has more than one.

state.description: An incident's own state, which `published` cannot express.

locale.description: The language this piece is DECLARED to be written in, as canonical BCP-47: language lowercase, script title case, region uppercase (`es`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hant`, `es-419`) — never an underscore form. `null` when nobody declared a language for this piece; it is never filled in from the space's or the organization's default, so a value is always a fact about this piece. A page reports what was declared for it, else its translation's language when it is a language twin (twins of the primary version are listed as items of their own); a source page is `null` until declared. A topic (post, forum topic, release, roadmap card) and an incident report what was declared for them — their translations are served under the piece's own id, not listed as items. Correct it with `PATCH …/items/{itemId}` `{ "locale": "es" }`: that moves `updatedAt` and never changes `contentHash`. Absent on a tombstone.

updatedAt.description: When this piece last changed. What the walk is ordered by, and what `updated_since` compares against.

url.description: Where a reader can see it, or null when the space is not published to an address. Never guess this: a null means "not published", which is a different thing from "we guessed wrong".

contentHash.description: A hash of the content itself, present when `include` was asked for. Diff a whole space from one list request without transferring a body.

deleted.description: Set on a piece that has been removed. See `include_deleted`.

sections.description: Markdown per named slot, when `include=sections` was asked for.

markdown.description: The whole piece as markdown, when `include=body` was asked for.

contentIn.description: WHICH of the two fields above holds this piece's content. Present on every row that carries content. `sections` is populated only for a piece written against a shape; a free-form piece returns `sections: {}`, which a client cannot otherwise tell from a piece that is genuinely empty. Check this rather than assuming: asking for `include=sections` alone on a space of free-form pieces yields nothing and looks like success.

freshness.description: Whether this is still known to be true. Absent on a tombstone and on an incident, which is a record of something that happened and does not go stale.

items.description: The pieces, and nothing else. No cursor, no total, no watermark — this shape cannot express a walk, which is why it is the one being retired.

ItemListLegacyDto.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

checkpoint.description: Store verbatim and send back as `updated_since`. The server defines the watermark so no client has to reason about clock skew.

items.description: Absent from `2027-01-01`: read `data`.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

xp.description: The xp this was derived from (clamped ≥ 0).

currentLevelXp.description: The threshold at which the current level began.

nextLevelXp.description: The next level threshold, or null at the cap.

xpIntoLevel.description: xp accrued since the current level began.

xpForNextLevel.description: xp the current level spans, or null at the cap.

progression.description: Progression per track. Phase 1 has only the shared `default` track.

points.description: The weighted-points total the level is derived from (xp == points).

entitlements.description: Feature/quota gates. Empty in Phase 1 (extension point).

directives.description: Imposed policy (bans, read-only). Empty in Phase 1 (extension point).

xp.description: The new xp total after the fold.

level.description: The level derived from the new xp.

levelChanged.description: True only when this grant moved the user across a threshold.

delta.description: xp actually added (0 on a replay / idempotent no-op).

name.description: Human label, if the grant supplied one.

delta.description: Signed amount actually applied (0 on an idempotent replay).

quantity.description: The quantity held after the fold.

delta.description: Signed quantity actually applied (0 on an idempotent replay).

HeaderIconName.description: Every icon name a `header` icon field accepts and the reader draws — the same list `GET /icons?for=header` serves.

PageIconName.description: Every icon name a `page` icon field accepts and the reader draws — the same list `GET /icons?for=page` serves.

CardIconName.description: Every icon name a `card` icon field accepts and the reader draws — the same list `GET /icons?for=card` serves.

details.description: Field-level validation problems, keyed by field path (422 only).

docs.description: Where the vocabulary or format this error is about is published — an absolute URL, or an API route such as `GET /space-types/{type}/presets`. Present on errors over a controlled list, so the answer to "what am I allowed to send?" is in the error itself.

reason.description: Why a credential was refused, as one stable word, where one status has several causes — e.g. an external_jwt redeem answers `iat_too_old`, `iat_in_future`, `bad_signature`, `bad_issuer`, `bad_audience`, `expired` and more. Branch on this, not on `message`.

slugs.description: The exact slugs that collided, on a slug-conflict 409 — `space.slug_taken`, `page.slug_taken`, `collection.slug_taken`, `site.slug_taken` or `badge.slug_taken`.

ops.description: The field operations since your `If-Match` that touch a path your own operations touch. Empty: none did — retry the batch unchanged under `etag`. `null`: the history no longer reaches your tag — re-read the entry first.

conflict.description: On a 409 from a content entry field write (`PATCH …/entries/{entryId}/fields`) whose `If-Match` was stale.

requestId.description: The id of this request — the same value as the `x-request-id` and `x-forumulate-request-id` response headers. Quote it in a bug report: it is the only thing that finds your exact request in our logs. It is in the body because that is the part that survives — an SDK that throws the parsed body, a serverless log that keeps the body and drops the headers, a ticket with the JSON pasted in.

Job.description: A background job in the shared model. `state` is one of `queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`; `result` is the feature’s answer once `completed`, `error` `{code, message}` once `failed`. Poll `links.self`, or wait with `forumulate jobs wait <id>`, or subscribe to `job.completed`.

BlockNode.description: One node of the document. `type` names the block or inline node — `paragraph`, `heading`, `bulletList`, `codeBlock`, `table`, `hint`, `image`, `text`, … — and `attrs`/`content`/`text`/`marks` depend on it. `GET /docs/block-schema` returns the complete union: every node type, its attributes, which are required, and the values an enumerated attribute accepts. It is public, cacheable, and generated from the same schema this endpoint validates against, so it cannot drift from what a write will accept. Each block that has a Markdown spelling names it there (`directive`); `GET /docs/markdown-dialect` describes every directive.

type.description: The node kind, e.g. `paragraph`, `heading`, `codeBlock`, `text`. The full list is at `GET /docs/block-schema`.

attrs.description: Node-specific attributes, e.g. `{ "level": 2 }` for a heading.

text.description: The literal text, for a `text` node.

marks.description: Inline marks (bold, italic, link, …) on a `text` node.

BlockDoc.description: A page as a block document: TipTap/ProseMirror JSON, the canonical content model shared by the editor, the reader and the Markdown converters. Send this as `content` when creating a page or on `PUT /pages/{pageId}/content`. It is the shape `GET /pages/{pageId}/markdown` round-trips from. Author in Markdown instead by sending `body` (whole page) or `sections` (Markdown per named slot) — use exactly ONE of the three. Every block has a Markdown spelling: `:::name{attrs}` directives for callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns and buttons, listed at `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`.

content.text: Install the SDK, then create your first page.

ConsentPreset.description: The publishable (non-secret) vendor id. Exactly one field is REQUIRED, chosen by `provider`: `cookiemunch`→`cbid`, `cookiebot`→`cbid`, `onetrust`→`dataDomainScript`, `osano`→`customerId` (+ `configId`: Osano’s loader is `cmp.osano.com/<customerId>/<configId>/osano.js`, or both in `customerId` as `<customer>/<config>`), `termly`→`websiteUuid`. Saving a native provider without its id is a `422 validation.failed` naming the field (e.g. `preset.cbid`). `hosted`/`managed`/`none`/`inherit` take no preset.

cbid.description: CookieMunch site id / Cookiebot domain-group id.

customerId.description: Osano customer id — the first path segment of your osano.js URL.

configId.description: Osano configuration id — the second path segment of your osano.js URL.

FirstPartyAnalytics.description: Forumulate's OWN first-party measurement on the reader: page/topic/event/release views, form progress, search queries, A/B exposures and goals, call-to-action and affiliate clicks. `always` (the default): counted without asking while no consent manager is active — a cookieless, per-day aggregate deduped by a server-side hash; with an ACTIVE CMP it still waits for the visitor to grant `analytics` (`analytics_storage`). `with-consent`: counted only after an analytics grant, CMP or not. `off`: never counted. Resolved space → org → `always`; unset inherits.

AbTests.description: Whether the reader runs the page A/B tests (FOR-019). `on` (the default): each browser sees one arm, and the `fx_ab` arm cookie is written only once the visitor grants `statistics` (the same gate as `firstPartyAnalytics`). `off`: every reader sees the control arm and `fx_ab` is never written, so a consent manager without a statistics category needs none for Forumulate. Resolved space → site → org → `on`; unset inherits.

ConsentConfig.description: An org (or, inside a space `override`, a space) consent configuration. Attacker-influenced tenant input, validated hard: no free-text HTML anywhere, and a raw custom loader is accepted only from a host the org has verified.

provider.description: Which CMP renders the banner. `hosted` is our own banner; `managed` provisions a CookieMunch site under our key; `none` is essential-only; `custom` is bring-your-own.

custom.description: For `provider: custom` only. `adapterApi` opens a preference-centre URL (works anywhere); `loader` injects a raw vendor script, allowed ONLY when its host is a verified org domain.

loaderUrl.description: loader: the https loader URL; its host must be a verified org domain.

hosted.description: For `provider: hosted` — structured banner fields (categories, copy, links, theme). Never raw HTML.

webhookSecret.description: Write-only signing secret for this org's inbound consent/DSAR webhook. Set the secret your CMP issued, or POST `consent/webhook-secret` to mint one. Never returned by any GET.

oneOf.description: Inherit the org default CMP. `firstPartyAnalytics` and `abTests` may still be set for this space alone.
Override the org default wholesale (same shape as ConsentConfig plus `mode: override`).

SpaceConsentConfig.description: A per-space consent override: inherit the org default, or replace it.

ConsentConfigView.description: Admin view of the stored org config. Secrets never appear — only whether one is set, and whether a signed delivery has been verified.

status.description: Health signal. `active`: a provider is set with every id it needs. `misconfigured`: a provider is set but a required id is missing (a banner will NOT render). `inactive`: `none`/`inherit`/unset.

reason.description: Present when not fully active — why (e.g. `Missing required field preset.cbid …`).

webhookSecretSet.description: Whether an inbound-webhook signing secret exists.

webhookConfigured.description: TRUE once a correctly-signed delivery has been verified — proof the inbound loop works, not merely that a secret exists.

webhookVerifiedAt.description: When the last signed delivery verified.

webhookLastFailure.description: The last inbound delivery that did NOT verify (recorded at most once per 10 minutes), or null. `reason` is `bad_signature` (a signature header was sent but does not match the stored secret) or `missing_signature`. Each recorded failure is also an audit event `consent.webhook_failed`.

abTests.description: This space’s A/B switch, already resolved space → site → org → `on`.

firstPartyAnalytics.description: This space’s first-party measurement, already resolved space → org → default (`always`). The reader gates every Forumulate counter on it — and, whenever a CMP is active, on the visitor’s analytics grant.

scriptSources.description: The exact script origins the reader CSP + Trusted Types policy will allow for this provider.

dryRun.description: Present and true on a `?validate=true` response.

ConsentWebhookEvent.description: An inbound consent/DSAR event. A partner platform signs instead with its published Ed25519 key (`CookieMunch-Partner-Signature: t=<unix s>,kid=<kid>,ed25519=<base64url>` over `<t>.<raw body>`) and adds `linkId` and `externalId` (this organization's id or slug); its events are `consent.recorded`, `consent.withdrawn` and `ping`.

id.description: The event id (`evt_…`); a repeat of one already received is answered `duplicate: true`.

cbid.description: The site at the consent platform; must be one this organization configured.

crawlerBlocked.description: True when a CDN in front of the domain blocks an AI-crawler user agent (we probe with GPTBot). Says nothing about search-engine crawlers.

edgeCache.description: What a cache in front of this address does to a publish — see `verdict`.

message.description: One sentence describing the state and the next step.

mode.description: Where this domain is in claim → verify → activate. `unverified` — prove ownership first (TXT record, file or meta tag); `pending` — verified but not yet activated, so your own application still serves it (`POST …/activate` switches traffic), or activated moments ago with routing still settling; `dns` — a whole host whose DNS does not reach us yet (see `dns`); `path` — a subfolder domain that needs your reverse proxy (see `forward`); `verified` — live.

served.description: Whether readers are being served on this address right now.

age.description: How many seconds old the copy served was (`Age` header), or null when not sent.

cacheStatus.description: The cache status the CDN reported (lowercased), or null when it reported none.

detail.description: One sentence saying what to do about it.

heldPastOurTtl.description: True when the copy served was older than the TTL we asked for — the CDN is applying its own, longer TTL.

sMaxAge.description: The shared-cache TTL we asked for (`s-maxage`), to compare with `age`.

verdict.description: What a cache in FRONT of this address does to a publish. `direct` — no cache we can see, or only ours: a publish is live at once. `foreign-passthrough` — a CDN is in front but is not caching HTML, so it is harmless. `foreign-purgeable` — a CDN is caching HTML and the organization has given us credentials to purge it, so every publish purges it. `foreign-stale-risk` — a CDN is caching HTML and we cannot purge it: a publish reaches readers only when that cache expires. Fix it with a cache rule that bypasses HTML on this host, or by adding purge credentials.

PageInfo.description: The paging envelope a collection carries when the caller states `Forumulate-Version`. Each operation’s own response schema says whether it has one: a collection either carries `page`, or answers both this and its pre-envelope shape and picks by the header. No listing pages with keys of its own any more — the allowlists in openapi-collection-shape.test.ts are empty, which is what stops a new one from appearing. Read `hasMore` and `nextCursor`: the snake_case pair beside them is deprecated and is not sent to a caller who states `2026-11-01` or later.

limit.description: The limit this page was built with — what was asked for, capped. NOT the number of rows returned: a final page under the limit is normal, and `hasMore` is the only thing that says whether to keep walking.

hasMore.description: Whether another page follows this one.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to continue. Null on the last page.

has_more.description: The same value as `hasMore`. These two are the only snake_case keys in the API. Sent to callers who state `2026-09-01` or no version at all; ABSENT from `2026-11-01` onwards. Read `hasMore` instead — it is sent on every version.

next_cursor.description: The same value as `nextCursor`. Absent from `2026-11-01` onwards; read `nextCursor`.

total.description: Rows in the whole collection — the size of the set, not of this page, and not of what you have seen so far. ABSENT where the source cannot count the collection: the append-only logs (staff actions, automation runs, connector activity, ingested questions, chat history) grow without bound and are not counted on every page view. Walk on `hasMore`, which is exact on every answer; read `total` only to show a size, and handle its absence.

IdOrSlug.description: An identifier that may be written two ways: the uuid, or the slug — the readable name in the thing’s `slug` field, unique within its parent (an organization’s slug platform-wide; a space’s, site’s or library’s within its organization; a page’s, collection’s or category’s within its space). Responses always carry the uuid. A slug that names nothing is a 404 whose `error.param` names this parameter; a page slug several locale or version variants share is a 409 `reason: ambiguous_slug` (add `?locale=`/`?version=`, or send the uuid).

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and its OWN type’s namespace (`post` on a blog post, `changelog` on a release, `events` on an event, `roadmap`, `status` on an incident, `faq`/`careers` (+`docs`) on a question/role, `legal`, `contact`, `courses`, `forum`, `docs`; another type’s namespace is refused) — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

socialBadge.description: This piece’s badge on its generated social card, over the space’s `seo.socialCard.badge`: another `field`, literal `text` ("Sold out"), a `label`, or `hide: true` for no badge. `null` goes back to the space’s badge.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

alsoRedirectWww.description: Also answer `www.<hostname>` (same path) with a permanent redirect to this address, written into our proxy. Default false: a domain is registered for ONE hostname, so without it `www.acme.com/docs` reaches whatever else answers that name (often your own app, which 404s). Point the www name’s DNS where the bare name points; for a whole-host domain we also request its certificate.

minValue.description: Lowest number a voter may pick. With maxValue/step the range must span 2–20 steps.

maxValue.description: Highest number a voter may pick. Must be greater than minValue.

step.description: Spacing between pickable numbers (default 1). Widen it to keep the range inside 20 steps.

closesAt.description: When voting closes. Must be in the future — a past date created an already-closed poll.

sections.description: Slot key → markdown, as on `POST …/items`. Each slot named is replaced; slots not named are kept. A key this kind of piece has no slot for is a 422 naming the slots it has, and nothing in the request is applied.

locale.description: The language this piece is written in, as a BCP-47 tag (`es`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hant`, `es-419`); `null` clears the declaration. Stored and reported canonically. Moves `updatedAt` (so the piece reappears in `?updated_since=`) and never changes `contentHash`. Works on every kind — page, topic, incident. It does not move a page to another language address: a translation twin is created through the space's languages, not by relabelling.

Renaming a collection moves one address — its hub, `/c/<slug>` — and we write that rule for you; the pages filed under it are addressed by their own slug within the space and do not move.

from.description: The path to redirect FROM, relative to the space’s mount. A trailing `*` matches everything below it: `/old/*` matches `/old/a` and `/old/a/b`. The longest matching wildcard wins, and an exact rule always beats a wildcard.

to.description: Where to send it: a bare path (relative to this space’s mount) or an absolute `https://` URL, which means exactly what it says. A trailing `*` here carries the part the `from` wildcard matched — `/old/* → /new/*` sends `/old/a/b` to `/new/a/b`; without it, every match lands on the one address.

type.description: `redirect` (the default) sends the reader to `to`. `rewrite` serves `to` at the address that was asked for, without changing the URL. A rewrite names a path of this same space — an absolute `to` is refused, because a rewrite is not a proxy.

status.description: The redirect’s HTTP status: 301, 302, 307 or 308. Default 308 (permanent, keeps the method). Not allowed on a rewrite, which answers whatever `to` answers.

query.description: Query-string conditions. A map of key → exact value: every listed pair must be present for the rule to match (other keys are allowed). `"ignore"` — the default — matches whatever the query is. Among rules with the same `from`, the one with more conditions is tried first.

passQuery.description: `true` carries the incoming query string to the target (merged under any query the target already has); `false` drops it. Unset keeps it on a same-host redirect and drops it on an off-site one. A rewrite always keeps it.

blog.description: A BLOG space's settings, through `PATCH …/blog/settings`; the plan lists each key it moves.

forum.description: A FORUM space's settings, through `PATCH …/forum/settings`; the plan lists each key it moves.

careers.description: A CAREERS space's hiring configuration: `pipeline` (`PUT …/careers/pipeline`), `form` (`PATCH …/careers/form`), `ats` (the connected board — provider, board, syncEnabled; the API key stays in the console) and `indexing` (`{indexNow}`). Each part is planned and applied on its own.

maintenanceReminderHours.description: Hours before a scheduled maintenance window that confirmed subscribers are reminded of it (0 = never). Default 24. Only a window announced further ahead than this is reminded — one posted an hour before needs no reminder.

autoTranslate.description: Languages every incident is machine-translated into as it is posted and updated, with the organization’s own translation provider (Settings → DeepL). A translation a person wrote is never overwritten.

maintenanceReminders.description: Hours before a scheduled maintenance window that confirmed subscribers are reminded, up to three (72 and 1, say). Each is sent once. `[]` sends none. Replaces `maintenanceReminderHours`, which still reads back as the first.

maintenanceNotifyStart.description: Tell subscribers when a maintenance window starts. Default true.

maintenanceNotifyEnd.description: Tell subscribers when a maintenance window completes. Default true.

suppressAlertsInMaintenance.description: No operator alert (and no automatic incident) for a component while a maintenance window that affects it is in progress — the deploy that takes the health check down is expected. Default true.

smsTemplate.description: The SMS text sent to phone subscribers, with {page} {title} {state} {url} filled in. Null: the built-in line ("{page}: {title} — {state}. {url}").

replyTo.description: Where a subscriber's reply to a status email goes. Null: the organization's mail default.

alertChannels.description: Which channels readers may subscribe through, each on (default) or off. A channel switched off is not offered on the page, a new subscription through it is refused, and existing ones stop receiving notices.

uptimeExcludesMaintenance.description: Maintenance is not downtime (default true). False: a maintenance window costs the days of the manual components it affects like an outage does.

dayThresholds.description: This page's own day-colour floors: a day on the uptime bar is operational at or above `operational`%, partial at or above `partial`%, an outage below. `null` clears them so the page follows the org's `status.day_thresholds` (default 99.9 / 99). One failed check never moves a day off operational on its own.

stateSource.description: Where this page's component states come from. `current`: the latest checks — what every reference status page reports; the uptime window stays on the page as the percentage and the bars. `window`: the latest checks, then a poor uptime window degrades a passing check (under 99.5% degraded, under 97% partial outage). `null` clears it so the page follows the org's `status.state_source` (default `current`).

status.description: A STATUS space's settings, through `PUT …/status/settings` (keys left out are kept).

settings.description: Merged into the space (`PATCH …/spaces/{id} {settings}`), STRICT: an unknown key is refused by name. `blog`, `forum` and `status` are the type's own settings doors.

compare.description: A COMPARE space's catalog (products, criteria, the matrix of `values`, scoring, freshness, naming), merged per top-level key like `PATCH …/compare/catalog`; `matrix` is the matrix as CSV text, laid over the catalog like `PUT …/compare/catalog.csv`. Judged by the catalog schema at planning. Comparison pages are `pages[]` entries with `metadata.comparison`.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

sections.description: Markdown per section of the piece, keyed by the section key its shape declares. A BLOG article ships two, BOTH REQUIRED: `standfirst` (the line listings and link previews show) and `body` (the post). A space can add or rename its own — the keys for one are at `GET /space-types/{type}/slots` (and the space’s own shape). Combined with `markdown`, which follows the sections as ordinary prose.

onThisPage.description: Whether THIS piece carries the "on this page" rail: `auto` (the surface default), `always` or `never`. Beats the space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` clears it back to the space’s.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

ipAllowList.description: IP addresses and CIDR blocks that may READ this address — `203.0.113.7`, `203.0.113.0/24`, `2001:db8::/32`. An empty list means anywhere, which is what every domain has by default. Enforced before a page is rendered, against the client address the edge resolved; an entry that is not an address or a block is a 422, because one that nothing can parse would never match and would lock out the world silently.

state.description: How far `apply` takes the domain — a MINIMUM, forward only: a domain already further along is never walked back (an `active` domain declared `verified` stays active). `claimed` (the default): the domain is added and held; `manual` lists the ownership TXT record (and the `.well-known` file) to publish. `verified`: ownership is checked (`verify` with `activate: false`) and traffic is NOT switched — your own application keeps serving the address. `active`: verified, then activated — we start answering it. The steps run in order, verify → activate. When no proof is served yet, `onUnverified` decides: `hold` (the default) keeps the domain claimed, reports the step `waiting` with what each proof method saw, and carries on with every other unit — the next apply takes it forward; `fail` stops the run there. A plan reports the same `waiting` before anything is written. A step that just activated reports `settling: true`: routing takes about a minute and `GET …/setup` may answer `pending` (`pendingReason: settling`) meanwhile.

onUnverified.description: When `state` is `verified` or `active` and the ownership proof is not served yet: `hold` (the default) keeps the domain claimed, reports the step `waiting: <what each proof method saw>` and carries on with every other unit (the apply exits 0; re-apply once the file is served); `fail` stops the run at this domain, as before.

signInUrl.description: Your own sign-in page (https). When set, the reader sign-in surface shows one "Sign in to continue" link to this URL instead of the provider buttons (an Atlas provider keeps its own sign-in page), with these query parameters appended: `returnTo` — the absolute URL of the page the reader was on (always set, replacing any `returnTo` already in the URL); `space` — the space slug; `spaceId` — the space id. **Your page must read `returnTo` and send the reader back there after sign-in**, for example `https://app.example.com/sign-in` receives `https://app.example.com/sign-in?returnTo=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.example.com%2Fguides%2Fintro&space=guides&spaceId=…`. A `{returnTo}` placeholder anywhere in the URL (`https://app.example.com/login?next={returnTo}`) is replaced with the URL-encoded address instead, and `returnTo` is then not appended again. `space`/`spaceId` are only added when the URL does not already carry them. readerAuth.description: How readers sign in, for the whole organization. externalRef.description: Your own name for this resource (printable ASCII, no spaces, ≤200). A repeat create naming a reference already held answers that resource (200, `idempotent: true`) instead of making a second one.

metadata.description: Free-form flat tags (≤50 keys; values string, number, boolean or null), filterable on the list with `?metadata[key]=value`. The older `metadata.forgedeck_ref` is still accepted as an alias of `externalRef`.

url.description: Where deliveries are POSTed. Must be https outside development, and is called with a signature header your receiver verifies — see the webhooks guide for the scheme.

events.description: The events this endpoint should hear, by name. At least one; `GET /webhooks/events` publishes the whole vocabulary with a sample payload for each.

format.description: The body shape. `json` (the default) sends our own event payload; `slack` and `discord` send a message that platform renders natively, so an incoming-webhook URL from either can be pasted in with nothing in between.

categoryIds.description: Narrow delivery to events whose payload names one of these forum categories. Omitted or null means no filter — the endpoint hears the event wherever it happens.

tagIds.description: Narrow delivery to events whose payload carries one of these tags. Omitted or null means no filter. Tags are matched by name, not by id.

groupIds.description: Narrow group, user and badge events to these groups. Omitted or null means no filter; it has no effect on events that name no group.

contentTypes.description: Narrow `content.*` events to entries of these content types (by key). Omitted or null means no filter. A model change to the whole model is always delivered.

locales.description: Narrow `content.*` events to entries in these locales (BCP-47 codes, or `default` for a space's source language). Omitted or null means no filter.

bodyEncoding.description: How the delivery body is encoded. `json` (the default) POSTs `application/json`; `form` POSTs `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, for a receiver that cannot parse JSON bodies.

signatureVersion.description: Which signature headers each delivery carries. `v1` is the timestamped scheme alone and is the default for a NEW endpoint; `both` adds the legacy body-only `sha256=`, which is replayable forever and exists only for receivers not yet migrated.

kind.description: `webhook` (the default) delivers signed events. `deploy_hook` sends a plain `POST` with an EMPTY body (no signature, no payload) to a Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages or Seolyticize deploy-hook URL, on `content.*` events and the publish events `page.published`, `page.live` and `topic.published` only. Debounced: Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare one call 30 s after the last change (at most 5 min after the first); Seolyticize one call 60 s after the last publish (at most 2 min after the first), per hook, so a 30-page apply is one call. The URL is write-only: reads answer its host and `/********`. Fixed at create.
