metadata.description: Free-form flat tags (≤50 keys; values string, number, boolean or null), filterable on the list with `?metadata[key]=value`. The older `metadata.forgedeck_ref` is still accepted as an alias of `externalRef`.

alertContacts.description: E-mail addresses told when this endpoint keeps failing: at 1 hour, at 24 hours, and when it is switched off. Up to 10. Omitted leaves them as they are; null or [] means the organization's owners.

alert_contacts.description: E-mail addresses told when this endpoint keeps failing: at 1 hour, at 24 hours, and when it is switched off. Up to 10. Omitted leaves them as they are; null or [] means the organization's owners.

kind.description: `http` (default) polls `url`; `heartbeat` waits for your job to ping; `manual` is probed by nothing — its state is `declaredState` (else operational) or what an open incident linked to it says; `space` rolls up another status page of this organization (`targetSpaceId`) on a hub page; `statuspage` mirrors a vendor’s public Statuspage (`url`, plus `vendorComponent`). Fixed at creation: a PATCH cannot turn one kind into another — delete and re-create instead.

targetSpaceId.description: Kind `space`: the status page it rolls up (state, uptime and days are that page’s).

vendorComponent.description: Kind `statuspage`: the vendor component’s id or exact name in its summary.json. Null: the vendor page’s overall indicator.

region.description: Where it runs ("EU", "US-East"). `theme.status.components.groupBy: region` groups by it.

description.description: What the component is, in a sentence — shown to readers beside its name.

slug.description: Its stable address within the page (component page, per-component subscription), normalised to lowercase words joined by hyphens. Minted from the name on create when omitted; unique per page — a taken one is a 409. Renaming the component does not move it.

linkUrl.description: Where the component’s own docs or product live; its name links there.

display.description: `bars` (default) draws its day bars; `status` only its state; `hidden-unless-degraded` leaves it off the page while it is operational.

startsOn.description: The day it started existing. Earlier days draw as "not yet" rather than as no data. Null: from its first check (a `manual` component: from the day it was created).

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds between checks (`http`, clamped to 30–3600, default 60) or the longest wait for a ping (`heartbeat`, clamped to 60–604800, default 3600). PATCH clamps by the same rule.

keywordAbsent.description: Invert `keyword`: the check FAILS while the term is in the body ("error", "maintenance mode") — Better Stack's "keyword absent". Default false.

probe.description: What a protocol monitor probes (kinds tcp, udp, icmp, dns, tls, smtp, imap, pop3, domain, browser): `host` (+ `port`), a DNS `record`/`resolver`/`expect`, the `days` a certificate or registration must have left, a browser check’s `url` and `selector`. Validated per kind; every host must resolve to a public address.

regions.description: Probe regions this component is checked from (`GET …/status/regions`). Empty: the primary checker only.

confirmRegions.description: How many regions must see it failing before it reads down (capped at how many report). Default 1.

barDays.description: Its own day strip length on the board; null follows the theme’s `bars.days`.

showUptime.description: Show its uptime figure beside the strip. Default true.

paused.description: Stop probing without deleting: the row and its history stay on the page, no new checks are taken and no alert is sent, and the component reads `unknown` (or its `declaredState`) until it is resumed. `alertsEnabled: false` only mutes the alerts while the probe keeps running.

audience.description: Who may see this on the public page: `everyone` (default), `signedIn` (any signed-in reader) or `groups` (a signed-in member of one of `groups`). Hidden rows are dropped by the API before anything is sent. The machine doors — `summary.json`, `api/v2`, the feeds, the badge and the widget — always answer as an anonymous reader.

declaredState.description: A state a person declares, which wins over the checks until it is cleared with `null`. Every field of this body — this one, `alertsEnabled` and both thresholds included — is applied on create exactly as on PATCH.

body.description: The whole page as a single Markdown string — the simplest way to author. Converted to blocks on write. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

sections.description: Markdown per named slot for a multi-slot page type, e.g. `{ "summary": "…md…", "steps": "…md…" }`. An undeclared slot name is a 422 naming the slots that exist.

config.description: Exactly what `PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/sites/{siteId}` takes as `config`, checked by that door.

readerIdentity.description: The org default reader-identity scope, `space` or `org`; shorthand for the `reader.identity_scope` org setting.

orgSettings.description: Organization settings by registry key (`GET /orgs/{orgId}/settings` lists them), each `PUT …/settings/{key}`.

servers.description: Replaces the spec’s root `servers` for this reference (ADV-8): the base URL its pages, curl samples and “Try it” use, and the origins the reader may call. untaggedTitle.description: The title of the page that operations without a tag are filed under. landingDescription.description: The landing page’s meta and `og:description`. Unset: the first sentence of the spec’s `info.description`, else a sentence naming the API, its operation count and its sections. Always overwrites; a derived description never overwrites one an author set by hand.

Saving it answers `warnings[]` (`sign_in_url_overrides_providers`, `signin_url_unreachable`, `sign_in_url_return_to_unconfirmed`).

signOutUrl.description: Your own sign-out page (https). whiteLabel.description: Hide Forumulate branding in the public readers and emails. Inside a site, the SITE theme’s `whiteLabel` (`config.theme.whiteLabel`) decides for every space in it.

chrome.description: Header and footer for a STANDALONE space. A space inside a site wears the SITE’s chrome (the top level of the site `config`) and this is stored but not rendered there.

cta.description: The call-to-action button at the end of the header row: `{ label, href }` plus its own colours and size. `ctas` (up to three) replaces it when set.

secondaryCta.description: A second header button beside `cta`, with its own style. `ctas` replaces both when set.

header.description: How the header bar looks and lays out its links: overlay, height, border, shadow, blur, logo, `linksAlign` (where `headerLinks` sit), `maxLinks` (how many before "More").

headerLinks.description: NAVIGATION — the header's own items, up to 12: `{ label, href }`, or an item that opens a dropdown (`children`) or a mega-menu panel (`panel`). In a site they REPLACE the automatic space tabs unless `headerSpaceIds` is set; how dropdowns open is `navMenu`, the phone/desktop behaviour is `mobileNav`/`desktopNav`.

navMenu.description: NAVIGATION — how the dropdowns and mega menus of `headerLinks` open (hover or click) and look. Items themselves live in `headerLinks`.

footerLinks.description: A flat row of footer links, up to 20 × `{ label, href }`. `footerColumns` is the multi-column footer.

footerDescription.description: A short blurb under the brand name in the footer, up to 400 characters.

footerColumns.description: A multi-column footer: up to 12 × `{ heading, links, stack }`, up to 20 links each (the link field is `label`).

socialLinks.description: Social profiles badged with icons in the footer, up to 10 × `{ platform, href }`.

copyright.description: The copyright or legal line at the very bottom of the footer, up to 200 characters.

footer.description: The footer's own lockup (`logo`, `logoMark`), where "Cookie settings" sits, your own footer HTML/CSS and a newsletter row.

mobileNav.description: NAVIGATION on a phone: `menu` (default — `headerLinks` behind a hamburger) or `bar` (inline in the header row). The wide-screen twin is `desktopNav`.

sticky.description: `true`: the header stays at the top while the reader scrolls. Default false.

align.description: The header row's arrangement: `split` (default — brand left, links right), `left`, or `center` (brand centred, links either side).

showSignIn.description: `false` takes the reader "Sign in" control out of the header (in-page sign-in prompts stay). Default true.

themeToggle.description: The light/dark control: `show`, `style`, `position` in the header row, colours.

sidebarBrand.description: The brand lockup at the top of the docs reader's left rail: `show` (default) or `hide`.

brandText.description: The brand's words beside the header logo: `auto` (default), `show` or `hide`, or the object form with `source` and `phone`.

logoPhone.description: `mark`: draw `logoMark` instead of the wordmark below 640px wide. Unset: the full lockup at every width.

accountMenu.description: What the signed-in reader's avatar menu holds: the entries and their order (built-ins and your own links), the name beside the avatar, the bell.

translations.description: The chrome in other languages: `{ "es": { labels: { "Pricing": "Precios" }, footerDescription, copyright } }` — `labels` maps the original words of any header item, footer link or button.

ctas.description: Up to three header buttons, in order. When set it replaces `cta` and `secondaryCta`.

topBar.description: NAVIGATION — a thin utility bar ABOVE the header row (an announcement, a few links, contact details). The header's main items are `headerLinks`; the row below it is `subnav`.

subnav.description: NAVIGATION — a section row BELOW the header row: your own `links` (and `endLinks`), and where a docs space with `sections.placement: "header"` draws its section tabs. The header's main items are `headerLinks`; the bar above it is `topBar`.

search.description: A search control in the header on every surface: `none` (default), `icon` or `pill`.

searchPlacement.description: Where the header search sits on a wide screen: `start`, `center`, `end` (default) or `before-links`.

searchHideOn.description: Hide the header search at one width: `["desktop"]` or `["phone"]`.

searchStyle.description: How the header search looks: the pill's words (also the placeholder), its fill and ink, size, and `glyph: false` to drop the magnifier.

desktopNav.description: NAVIGATION on a wide screen: `inline` (default — `headerLinks` in the bar) or `menu` (behind a menu button, as on a phone). The phone twin is `mobileNav`.

ForumulateVersion.name: forumulate-version
ForumulateVersion.description:
API version negotiation. **Send `forumulate-version: 2027-03-01` on every request** from a new integration; it is optional only so that integrations written before versioning keep working. Each version includes everything before it:

* `2026-09-01` — collections answer the paging envelope (`page`, `sync.checkpoint`, and `data` beside the named rows key).
* `2026-11-01` — `page` carries only `hasMore`/`nextCursor`, not the snake_case `has_more`/`next_cursor`.
* `2026-12-01` — three changes, one date: (1) a request-body field the operation does not recognise is a 422 naming its path on EVERY write (including inside a block document) instead of a 200 and `X-Unrecognized-Fields`; (2) a page whose slug is taken is a 409 unless you send `onSlugTaken: "suffix"`; (3) a new public space joins a site only when you send `siteId`.
* `2027-01-01` — the deprecated destruction aliases (`Space_purge`, `Page_purge`) refuse without `?confirm=<slug>`, exactly like `Space_destroy` and `Page_destroy` always do. Cache purges are `Cache_*`. And every paged list answers its rows once, under `data` (the named key is gone), without the document bodies (`markdown`, `sections`, `content`, `html`) unless `?include=` names them; `?fields=a,b` keeps only those keys of each row.
* `2027-02-01` — a search door (docs, reader, site, organization, chat and forum search) answers an EMPTY `q` with 422 `validation.failed` naming `q` and the minimum length, instead of a 200 with no hits. A short term still answers 200 with `minQueryLength`.
* `2027-03-01` — a reader token redeemed at `…/reader-auth/jwt` (or checked at `…/reader-auth/check`) with NO `email_verified` claim counts as UNVERIFIED, so it is never matched to an existing member by email. Earlier versions read an absent claim as verified.

Omit it and you receive the pre-envelope legacy response shape. Accepted values are dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` form; a malformed value is a 400, an unknown-but-date-shaped value rounds DOWN to the newest released version on or before that day (a day after the newest gets the newest; a day before the first gets the legacy shape). The `forumulate-version` response header always names the version served, and `forumulate-version-requested` echoes the date you sent when it was rounded.

On most READ operations this header changes nothing — they answer one shape to everybody. The operations that negotiate a shape are the ENVELOPED collections, and those are the ones whose responses carry `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` when you state no version; each declares all three as response headers, so look there rather than assuming. The pre-envelope shape is deprecated as of `2026-09-01` and is served until **2027-09-01**. After it, a request that states no version receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Nothing else is going away: the paths, the parameters and the error envelope are unaffected, and the operations themselves are not deprecated — only the shape, which is marked `deprecated` on the schema that is being withdrawn.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes this write safe to retry. **Optional** — send any unique string (a UUID is ideal) and the first request runs while its response is remembered under that key for 24 hours; an identical retry replays that same status and body instead of acting twice, so a timeout or a 5xx from the edge can be retried without creating a second row. A retry sent while the first request is still in flight is refused with `409`. The key is scoped to the method and path, so the same key on a different endpoint is a different request. Error responses of 5xx are never cached — those retries re-run. A key is bound to the BODY it was first used with: reusing it with a different body is a `409 idempotency.key_reused`, not a replay, because replaying would tell you a write landed that never ran. Generate one key per request, never per process or per session.

DryRun.name: dryRun
DryRun.description: `true`: authenticate, authorize and validate this request (body, query and path), then answer `200 {dryRun: true, ok: true, operation, checks}` WITHOUT carrying it out — nothing is written, queued, mailed or announced. It does not compute a diff, and a write that passes may still be refused by a state check at write time (a slug taken in between). Anything other than true/false is a 422.

LeanInclude.name: include
LeanInclude.description: From `2027-01-01`: the document bodies to keep in each row, comma-separated. An unknown name is a 422 naming the nearest one. Ignored by earlier versions, which always send the bodies.

LeanFields.name: fields
LeanFields.description: From `2027-01-01`: the only keys to return in each row, comma-separated (`id` always comes back; naming a body field brings it back). A name no row on the page carries is a 422 with a did-you-mean. Ignored by earlier versions.

Error400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

Error401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

Error403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

Error404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

Error409.description: Refused because of the state this already is in — a name or slug already taken, a resource that already exists, or a precondition on the thing itself (`conflict`, `*.taken`, `*.exists`). Unlike a 422 the body is fine; unlike a 503 retrying it unchanged will not help.

Error409_182d54.description: The slug is taken and `onSlugTaken: "fail"` was sent.

Error412.description: The precondition no longer holds: the resource changed after the tag you sent. Nothing was written. Re-read it, merge, and retry — the body names both tags (`precondition.failed`).

Error413.description: The archive or repository is over the import size limit. The message carries the limit; split the import or upload a ZIP of the subtree you want. A 422 here means the bytes could not be read as an archive at all, which is a different problem.

Error422.description: The body was understood and a value is unacceptable (`validation.failed`). `error.details` names the field paths.

Error429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

ErrorDefault.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.
